The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (2×2 ANOVA and contrasts) with peak coordinates and cluster-level inference, figures, and tables of results. Healthy adult results are reported separately (n=27 included in imaging analyses). Reporting of whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables satisfies the meta-analysis reporting requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment examining audiovisual integration of non-verbal social cues (animated faces and human non-verbal vocalizations), a clear social-related processing paradigm. The fMRI sample includes a healthy adult group (n=10, ages 24–37), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-by-voxel parametric t-tests, group activation maps, and cluster-correction procedures) and reports results in figures/tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Results for the healthy/control group are reported directly (not limited to a subgroup). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study includes healthy adult controls but focuses on seed-based task-dependent functional connectivity (gPPI) analyses and reports between-group comparisons; it does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails to meet the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task results and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants learned moral status (cooperator/defector) via interactive Prisoner’s Dilemma and were scanned while making gender judgments of those faces — a clear social-related task. The sample consists of healthy adults (scanned n=11, ages 21–36). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and tables/figures of activations. Results are not limited to ROI, connectivity, or between-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for task, sample, and whole-brain reporting.

This study is an fMRI trial of cognitive remediation in early-course schizophrenia patients (CET vs EST) using a cognitive control (POP) task. It does not include or report a healthy adult (age 18–65) control group or any whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps coming from healthy participants. The task examined is non-social (executive/cognitive control), not a social-processing paradigm. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirements for (1) inclusion of healthy adult participants and (2) reporting a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Exclusion criterion E4 applies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Theory of Mind; false-belief vs false-photo), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=25) aged 18–59, meeting the 18–65 criterion. The authors report whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (FB > FP) and explicitly state they derived functional ROIs/masks from the control group data (i.e., a control-group FB>FP map), with FWE-corrected results and figures/tables referenced; thus whole-brain healthy-group task effects are available. Results are reported in the main text and supplemental materials. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group task map, out-of-age-range, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used task-based paradigms involving processing of emotional facial expressions (social perception/communication). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=9, mean age 27±7) and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons and task-related activations attributed to controls (text, figures and tables with coordinates describing control activations and diagnosis × task interactions). Whole-brain, voxelwise results are reported and described (with Talairach coordinates and cluster-level findings), satisfying reporting via tables/figures/text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, or missing healthy-group whole-brain maps) apply. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. Participants (n=17, ages 20–36) were healthy adults, satisfying sample criteria. The task involved social scenarios and face identity processing (social-related constructs: perception/understanding of others), and fMRI data were acquired during task performance. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 random-effects ANOVAs) with whole-brain thresholds and cluster-corrected results, plus tables/figures of activations and stereotactic coordinates; small-volume corrections are additionally reported. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from a healthy adult group. No exclusion criteria apply.

This article is a Personal View / review paper discussing mirror neuron dysfunction in autism spectrum disorders and summarizes evidence from fMRI, TMS, and EEG. It does not report original empirical fMRI data from healthy adult participants nor present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy/control group. Therefore it fails the requirement for original whole-brain task activation data. It is a non-empirical paper rather than an fMRI study meeting inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 24.4) that investigates processing of angry prosody—a social-communication/emotion perception task—using a dichotic listening paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, whole-brain contrasts) with coordinates and cluster results for healthy participants. Results for the healthy sample are presented directly (not only subgroup or connectivity analyses). Thus it meets the meta-analysis focus on fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and satisfies whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an emotional face recognition paradigm (social perception) in healthy adult participants (N=116, males, mean age 24.7). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (familywise-error–corrected voxelwise statistics with peak coordinates and cluster sizes; whole-brain regression analyses are described), and results for the healthy sample are clearly presented. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for task domain, participant sample, and whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-adult sample, non-empirical) apply.

The study reports event-related fMRI during perception of others' emotional facial expressions, a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). Participants are 14 healthy right-handed adults (mean age 29±6), within 18–65. The abstract states statistical parametric mapping identified activation in dorsal medial frontal cortex, indicating group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses; results are described in the text (and likely reported in figures/tables). Thus the paper meets requirements for fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (perception and understanding of others’ identity and emotion from voices) during task performance, meeting I3. The sample includes a healthy adult sighted group (n=15, mean age ~32), meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (univariate contrasts and multivariate searchlight MVPA) and provides group-level statistical maps and cluster tables; group effects and within-group decoding results for the sighted are described, satisfying I5 and I6. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and cluster coordinates in figures and tables, and analyses include unbiased ROI and whole-brain searchlight approaches. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

Although the study uses fMRI in healthy adult participants and includes social cognition tasks (theory-of-mind and attribution-of-attention), it does not report a group-level, whole-brain (unmasked) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. The analyses use localized, ROI-based ICA restricted to a temporoparietal mask to identify task-related independent components and report seed-to-voxel connectivity maps, but no unmasked whole-brain voxelwise activation contrast (GLM) is provided. Therefore it constitutes an ROI-focused analysis without whole-brain task activation results, violating the review’s whole-brain evidence requirement.

The study reports task-based fMRI of self- and other-reflection (social cognition: perception/understanding of self and others), includes a healthy adult control group (n=33) aged within 18–65, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation results for the control group (Self>Facts, Other>Facts, Other>Self) with cluster-level correction. Whole-brain maps and supplementary tables for the control group are described, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. It is empirical fMRI task data (not resting-state or connectivity-only) and healthy-group results are clearly reported separately from the clinical group.

This article is a theoretical/review paper discussing explanations for mirror-touch synesthesia and does not report original empirical fMRI data or methods/results from healthy adult participants. The abstract indicates conceptual/theoretical discussion and cites existing fMRI evidence but provides no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps from a healthy control group, nor any reported task-based fMRI methods/results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=31 analyzed) investigating social perception of others (neural and behavioural responses to facial disfigurement; relevant to perception/understanding of others and stigma). The fMRI analysis includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SnPM nonparametric group analysis with familywise error correction and cluster-level reporting) comparing pre- vs post-surgery faces, with results presented as whole-brain activation/deactivation clusters. Participant ages (18–35) fall within the 18–65 range. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults are met.

This empirical fMRI study investigates humor processing—a social cognitive/emotional process involving perception and understanding of others (ToM/ social cognition). It used task-based whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) reporting group-level contrasts (Cartoons vs Neutral, parametric modulation) with corrected statistics and conjunctions, and provides tables/figures of results. The sample comprises 29 healthy adult participants (mean age 27, range within 18–65). Reporting includes whole-brain maps/coordinates. Therefore it satisfies the review’s task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (risky decisions in social scenarios) reporting task-evoked neural activations. The sample includes a young adult group (30 young adults) in addition to late adolescents, satisfying the requirement of a healthy adult group. The abstract reports whole-brain task activation results (voxelwise activations described across multiple cortical and subcortical regions such as OFC, MTG, PCC, precuneus, insula, IFG, pre-SMA, caudate, STS), indicating group-level whole-brain evidence for the healthy group. Results for the age groups are reported separately (activations “for both age groups” and group comparisons), and whole-brain results are described in the text/tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines how collective (social) schemas shape memory representations. The task involved participants recalling museum pictures and analysing neural patterns related to collective/social knowledge (dmPFC/vmPFC). The sample consists of 24 healthy adults aged 22–39. The paper reports whole-brain searchlight analyses with group-level correction (TFCE, permutation testing) and presents whole-brain results (Extended Data Fig. 1), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and satisfies the listed inclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI task in which subjects viewed others’ actions (perception/understanding of others), a construct falling under social-related processing (I3). The paper identifies specific brain regions (pSTS, MT/MST, EBA) showing action-specific adaptation effects, indicating group-level task-evoked effects rather than only ROI or connectivity results, consistent with whole-brain voxelwise activation reporting (I5, I6). Although participant demographics are not detailed in the provided excerpt, this is an empirical fMRI study of healthy adult volunteers published in J Cogn Neurosci, and the described results are presented for the healthy group, satisfying the sample criterion (I4). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in which healthy adult participants (n=36) performed an Other task requiring prediction of another person’s decisions—clearly a social-related task (simulation/theory-of-mind). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (significant clusters reported with corrected p-values and Talairach coordinates; Tables and figures show whole-brain results) based on the healthy participant group. Results for the healthy/control group are presented (behavioral and fMRI within-group effects). Reporting includes coordinate tables and figures consistent with whole-brain maps. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI social-processing studies in healthy adults.

This fMRI study investigates the neural basis of understanding others' actions via the auditory mirror system—directly addressing social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The experiment used task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (11 subjects in the fMRI subgroup; mean age 24.2) and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM5; cluster-level correction) with statistical maps and tables/figures. Whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the healthy group are clearly described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults and does not violate listed exclusions.

Study uses task-based fMRI of prosodic speech perception, which is a social-communication related process (affective/pragmatic prosody). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=8, mean age ~23) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the control group (one-sample t-tests, conjunctions, and contrasts) with thresholding and anatomical localization. Results for controls are clearly described (activation and deactivation maps). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining mind perception (a social-cognitive process) using event-related fMRI during a mind-perception task and a separate behavioral gaze-cueing task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=22; mean age 24.4), meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric regressors, FLAME1), with cluster-corrected whole-brain results and peak coordinates (e.g., significant vmPFC clusters) and figures/tables describing these maps. Thus it provides healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation maps in formats acceptable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (viewing realistic first-person social interaction videos) in a healthy adult sample (n=20 males, mean age 24.6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected thresholds) with peak coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Behavioral and imaging results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of perception of facial expressions (social communication/perception of others), using a task involving viewing facial expressions during fMRI. Participants were healthy adults (n=24, mean age 25.2). The authors performed group-level mixed-effects analyses and generated parameter estimate maps for each expression and registered them to MNI space; additionally a group-level faces>scrambled (localiser) contrast was used to define whole-brain face-selective ROIs. Thus the paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps from healthy participants and meets the review’s reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of communicative interaction (social communication) in healthy adult participants (54 right-handed males, ages 18–27). The task probes social-related processing (establishment of mutual understanding) and uses task-evoked fMRI with whole-brain group-level analyses (reported contrasts, parametric modulations, and cluster-level inference), including anatomical localization and coherence analyses. Whole-brain results are described in the main text and figures (with supplementary materials), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, healthy adult group reported separately). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates learning about others’ preferences and social influence on inter-temporal choice, using a social-related task (delegated decisions for novel and familiar others) in healthy adult participants (mean ages 23.6 and 25.6; adults 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects second-level analyses, cluster-defining thresholds and FWE correction) with reported coordinates and figures. Results and contrasts for healthy/control participants are clearly described. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task and an age-judgement control), includes a well-characterized healthy adult control group (n≈24, ages 18–59), and presents group-level whole-brain activation results for the healthy controls (described in the text and Supplementary Table S2) using FWE-corrected voxelwise analyses. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and inference (voxelwise Z threshold and cluster correction), and the paper explicitly reports healthy-control activation patterns, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain, task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (effortful control of interpersonal trust/distrust) in healthy adult participants (n=59–60, mean age ~20, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., trust > age, distrust > age, and combined contrasts) with family-wise error correction and provides tables/figures and MNI coordinates. Whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly reported in the text/tables/figures, and ROI analyses are supplementary but do not replace whole-brain results. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, mean age 35.9) that explicitly manipulates a social interaction (human–human vs human–machine competition) to engage Theory of Mind/social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (contrasts such as [H(I+C)>M(I+C)], [I(H+M)>C(H+M)], interaction [H(I>C)]>[M(I>C)]) with voxelwise thresholding (P<0.001 uncorrected) and tables/figures listing activated clusters and Talairach/MNI coordinates. Results for the healthy sample are presented clearly. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked maps reported (tables and figures).

The study used task-based fMRI during a validated social cognition paradigm (Animated Triangles / HCP social cognition task), includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (N=25) analyzed separately, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and peak coordinates for the healthy controls (FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates are provided). Whole-brain results for the healthy group are described in text, figures, and coordinates. Although the paper also reports DCM/effective connectivity and a clinical group, these do not preclude inclusion because the healthy-group whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is a task-based fMRI hyperscanning study of joint attention and mutual gaze (social interaction, social communication/perception). Participants: healthy adult volunteers (ages reported, n provided). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (tables of coordinates, cluster-level FWE-corrected results, figures) clearly from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are described in text and tables. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based fMRI of gesture-speech integration, a social-communication process. It includes healthy adult participant groups (H-group: n=19, ages 19–32; C-group: n=17) reported separately from clinical participants. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results for the healthy/control group (e.g., conjunction and contrasts with MNI coordinates and significance values; Supplementary Table 2), not just ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides usable whole-brain results.

This paper is a narrative/review article (REVISIÓN) on ecstatic and related neurological phenomena, not an empirical fMRI study. It does not report original fMRI data from healthy adult participants performing social-related tasks, nor does it present group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables for a healthy/control group. The topic focuses on seizures, Stendhal syndrome, and autoscopic phenomena rather than social-processing tasks. Therefore it violates the requirement for original fMRI data in healthy adults and meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical review without original fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based functional MRI while participants performed a social-affective judgment task (rating emotions evoked by images of social groups), directly addressing social perception/understanding of others. Participants were healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 19.5), satisfying the sample-age criterion. The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and contrast results (e.g., mPFC, insula, amygdala activations) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Results are reported as whole-brain effects (Talairach coordinates, t-values) and in-text contrasts, fulfilling the reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The task involved listening to human footsteps and reporting motion direction, which constitutes perception of others’ actions (a form of social-related processing: Perception and Understanding of Others). The study used fMRI in healthy adults (10 participants aged 20–29) and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., ‘footstep minus rest’) with random-effects analysis and supplementary maps/tables. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for a social-related fMRI task in healthy adults and provides whole-brain healthy-group results.

This is an fMRI study of theory-of-mind/false-belief processing in healthy adults (mean age 22.7) using task-based fMRI while participants watched Sally–Anne movies (social-related task). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts are reported (belief > photo/map; implicit false- > true-belief) with SPMs and peak coordinates. Results for the healthy adult sample are presented separately. Thus all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI of Theory-of-Mind (visual joke) — a social cognition paradigm (meets I3). It includes a healthy control group of adults (n=13) matched for age and IQ (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and within-group contrasts (ToM vs Physical) with tables/figures and thresholding/cluster correction, including results attributable to the control group (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (n=12, ages 20–32) that investigates person-related (social) conceptual processing (learning facts about people vs buildings/hammers). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses (person > building AND person > hammer), with cluster-size correction and whole-brain maps and supplemental tables of results and connectivity. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-related task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level voxelwise task results (I5), and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in figures/tables/supplement (I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social task (Trust Game) examining social decision-making (I3); the sample is healthy adults aged 19–30 with group-level results reported separately (I4); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., GAME>CONTROL, INVESTOR>CONTROL, TRUSTEE>CONTROL) with coordinates and tables (I5); whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures and table of coordinates (I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 21–48) using erotic picture/video stimuli depicting other people, which falls under social-related constructs (Perception and Understanding of Others). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (one-sample contrasts within each healthy orientation group, with FWE-corrected maps and cluster reports) alongside ROI analyses. Whole-brain results are clearly described and presented in figures/tables. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis criteria for fMRI social-related tasks in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (vitality forms of speech and action), conducted in 18 healthy adult participants (mean ages ~25). The paper reports group-level task-evoked whole-brain analyses (contrasts Vitality vs Control) with cluster- and peak-level FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates (tables/figures), as well as conjunctions and PPI analyses. Whole-brain activation maps/coordinates are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates social-related processing (cognitive and emotional empathy) using the Multifaceted Empathy Test, satisfying the social-task requirement. The sample includes healthy adult control participants reported separately from the BPD group (female controls, presumably adults within 18–65), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results for the healthy/control group (main effects and within-group contrasts are presented in tables and figures with MNI coordinates), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported as coordinates/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, or lack of healthy-group whole-brain maps) are violated.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (ages 18–35), using task-evoked olfactory self-assessment (‘would you like to smell like this?’) that probes perception/understanding of self, a social-related construct. Group-level, within-group (healthy participants) second-level contrasts were conducted (e.g., ‘self’-peptide minus solvent; ‘self’-peptide minus ‘non-self’-peptide) with activation coordinates reported in MNI space (right middle frontal cortex) and statistical thresholds described. The paper states that whole-brain analysis was performed and presents voxelwise activation coordinates and corrected p-values; results are clearly identified for the healthy group. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI of social-related processing in healthy adults and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not resting-state, and participants are within 18–65).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 22.9; 15 subjects included) using a social interaction/provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes social processing (reactive aggression, perception/response to others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with GLMs, statistical maps, coordinate tables and figures (thresholds and cluster sizes provided), and results are clearly from the healthy participant group. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample) apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI during a social-norm inference task (social-related processing). It includes a healthy adult control group (22 TD males, ages 18–35) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts/maps (e.g., all-stimuli vs fixation, visual and auditory GLM contrasts) for the control group and describes statistical results and voxelwise activations. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Trust Game) and reports neural correlates, but the sample consists of adolescents across three developmental phases rather than healthy adults (18–65). No subgroup of healthy adults is reported separately. Therefore it fails the sample inclusion criterion (I4) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (participants only outside the 18–65 range).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of personal (social) familiarity and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the healthy control group, the healthy participants are described as "healthy elderly"/older adults rather than adults in the 18–65 range required by the review. No subgroup of healthy participants aged 18–65 is reported separately. Therefore the study violates the age-range inclusion requirement and must be excluded (E5).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a facial emotion discrimination task (socially relevant processing of others’ emotional expressions). Participants are healthy adults aged 19–35 with a clearly defined normal control (NC) group reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results (cluster tables and FWE-corrected maps) for within-group contrasts and condition effects in the NC as well as between-group contrasts; ROI results are supplementary but whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy control group are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adult subgroup, empirical fMRI task data).

This is a task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion recognition (socially relevant stimuli: angry, fearful, etc.) in healthy adult males (age 21–33). The paper reports group-level whole-brain (whole-slab) analyses with activation maps and voxelwise results (thresholds reported, figures shown) and provides coordinate-based results for several regions, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus criteria for fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group results are met.

This is an fMRI study of healthy young adults (ages 21–24) that includes a social manipulation (peer observation) during task performance, addressing social-related processing (social influence/mentalizing). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results for both the Go/No-Go and Stoplight tasks (traditional subtraction analyses) and provides thresholded/unthresholded maps in NeuroVault. Although the paper emphasizes seed-based connectivity analyses, it also presents whole-brain activation maps and contrasts for the healthy participant group. Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range and results for this group are reported separately. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task fMRI of social processing (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the full text reports primarily between-group contrasts (BPD vs NSSI and conjunctions vs HC) and does not present or clearly describe an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (within-group/ main effect) for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criterion I5 requires a healthy-group whole-brain map (or equivalent tabulated coordinates/figure) clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Because the paper only reports between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effect, it meets exclusion criterion E4.

The study uses task-based fMRI of emotional facial expression processing (a social-communication/social-perception task) in 12 healthy subjects and reports task-evoked BOLD signal increases across many brain regions (implicit and explicit contrasts), consistent with whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Although exact participant ages are not reported in the provided text, participants are described as healthy subjects (implying adults). Therefore the study meets the social-related fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain results criteria.

The study used task-based fMRI to examine perception of face gender, which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (a social-related construct). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 19–42) with group results reported for the healthy sample. Importantly, the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxel-wise random-effects analyses (gender-different > gender-same), with cluster-corrected maps and reported activated clusters/coordinates, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. ROI analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study used task-based fMRI of social processing (script-driven interpersonal rejection and imagined aggression) and included a healthy adult control group (female adults 18–65), the paper reports whole-brain functional connectivity analyses and group differences in connectivity rather than presenting any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group. The standard activation results were noted as reported in prior work, but this full text does not provide unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effects (voxelwise maps or coordinate tables) required by the review. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group results and must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 24.4) that investigates social-context modulation of empathy for others' pain. The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others' pain/intentionality). The paper reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts (main effects and interactions) with coordinates and FDR-corrected results across the healthy sample. Results are presented in tables and figures and report group-level activation maps and PPI connectivity, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses task-based fMRI to investigate emotional prosody processing — a social-communication / perception task — in adults. It includes a healthy control group of adults (age range 20–46) reported separately from the ASD group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (e.g., emotional vs. neutral prosody) with cluster-level FWE correction and reports activations for controls and conjunction maps; results are presented as whole-brain contrasts and coordinates. Although the study also reports PPI effective connectivity, it does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity analyses. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI social-related task data in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a dynamic facial-expression localizer, i.e., a social perception task targeting perception/understanding of others. The paper reports selection of a posterior STS cluster across subjects based on contrasts of dynamic facial expressions versus static faces and moving dots, indicating group-level voxelwise task activation (GLM/RFX language appears in the text). Participants are described in the context of future clinical application (ASD) but the study itself used healthy subjects and reports results across subjects. Therefore the study provides whole-brain, task-evoked activation maps for a healthy adult group and meets the review’s social-processing fMRI criteria.

The study used fMRI and included a healthy adult control group and reported whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the control group (so I4, I5, I6 are satisfied). However, the experimental task was a continuous performance task with monetary reward (reward processing), not a social-related task (no social interaction/communication or perception-of-others paradigm). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task) required by the review objective. No exclusion criteria E2–E6 directly apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–60) that investigates social-related processing (observation of mouth actions, social communication, empathy). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM analyses, FWE-corrected maps, tables of coordinates and figures) for within-group and between-group contrasts. Thus it satisfies the fMRI social-task criterion, healthy adult sample criterion, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

The study does not investigate social-related processing: fMRI tasks used are verbal associative fluency and Hayling sentence completion (verbal executive and response-inhibition tasks), which do not probe social communication, affiliation/attachment, or perception/understanding of self/others. Although the study includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~27) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy controls (satisfying I4, I5, I6), it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task). Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of self/other social cognition (trait judgments), using healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 24.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and statistical parametric maps with tables of coordinates and figures (SPM analyses, whole-brain thresholds described). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level results (I5), and allowance for coordinate/figure reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 19–39) that investigates social/kinship processing and moral decision-making using movie-viewing and a moral-dilemma task. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from both inter-subject correlation (ISC) analyses during movie viewing and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task, including figures, cluster tables, and unthresholded maps available on NeuroVault. The study population, tasks, and reported whole-brain maps directly address social-related processing in healthy adults and meet the review’s requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This study reports task-based functional MRI of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception) in healthy adults (ages 18–32). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., faces associated with behaviors vs. novel faces; negative vs. positive; disgust vs. aggression) with Talairach coordinates, cluster volumes, and statistical thresholds reported in tables and figures. Results for the healthy/control sample are reported separately and not limited to ROIs; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior) in healthy adult participants (N=32, females, mean age 22.7). The tasks are social-cognitive (mentalizing, empathy for pain, prosocial decision), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., Mentalizing > baseline; Dissimilar > Similar; Painful > Non-Painful) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of coordinates/results. Healthy adult sample and separate reporting of healthy-group results are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social evaluation (perception/understanding of others) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–29). The task is social (forced-choice judgments about target persons across situations) and uses task-evoked BOLD fMRI. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (multilevel whole-brain MLM, cluster coordinates and figures; supplementary tables reported) and ROI follow-ups, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an fMRI study that investigates naturalistic theory-of-mind/social cognition using a video-based task (ToM vs physical inference). It reports results for a healthy adult control group (n=22; analyses reported for the control group separately) within the adult age range (18–65). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (ToM > physical inference) with family-wise error cluster-corrected activations and tables of coordinates for the mentalising network in the control group (see Table 3 and figures). Whole-brain within-group task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, resting-state, or non-empirical-only reporting).

Full text not accessible and available information (title and citation) indicates a study of first-episode schizophrenia. There is no evidence in the provided content that (1) a healthy adult control group (age 18–65) is included and reported separately, or (2) that the paper reports at least one whole-brain, group-level task activation map for a healthy/control group. Because these required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be confirmed from the supplied information, the study must be excluded. The most relevant exclusion criterion is E4 (no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported or cannot be confirmed).

This is an fMRI study of social evaluation in a healthy adult sample (meets I3 and I4). However, all reported group-level effects were restricted to a bilateral vACC region-of-interest and small-volume–corrected within that ROI. The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map or whole-brain coordinates for healthy participants; results focus on ROI-corrected clusters. Therefore it fails the requirement for reporting whole-brain healthy-group task activation and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–34) that uses a passive action observation task probing action perception/understanding (mirror system) — a social-related construct. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts, thresholded and reported with coordinates and peaks) for the healthy control groups and describes results across mirror system areas. Therefore it meets the fMRI social-processing task requirement, the healthy adult sample requirement, and provides whole-brain group-level task activation maps clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (mentalizing/understanding others via the why/how task and default-mode network activation). Participants were healthy adult humans (n≈27–28, ages 21–33), meeting the age/sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and conjunction analyses, with cluster-extent correction, coordinates, tables and figures (Study 1 whole-brain results and Study 2 ROI + whole-brain confirmation). Results for the healthy/control group are reported separately and clearly. It is not an ROI-only, resting-state, nor clinical-only study. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical) with tables of significant regions, corrected thresholds, and figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Behavioral and imaging methods, participant characteristics, and univariate and multivariate analyses are fully described for the healthy sample. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (modified Trust Game) directly probing reciprocity/trust (social-related processing). The sample comprised healthy adult participants aged 18–30 (reported group-level results for the healthy sample). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrasts (GLM one-sample/t-tests with cluster correction) and provides tables/figures of activation coordinates. Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures satisfies the meta-analysis reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-adult sample) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (mental state attribution/intentional stance) in healthy adults. The analyzed sample (N=12; ages 21–31) is within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Composer > Computer) entered into a second-level random-effects analysis, with coordinates and cluster thresholds provided (tables and figures). Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Behavioral and imaging results directly target perception/understanding of others, meeting the meta-analysis objectives.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related emotional face matching task and includes a healthy adult control group (ages 21–64). However, it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The paper reports whole-brain group×drug interactions and a task activation map collapsed across group and drug (Supplementary Fig. S2), but no standalone voxelwise healthy-group task map or within-control main effect map is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (male, ages 18–30) performing a social interpersonal-distance task (affiliation/personal space). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected results, main effects and treatment×protagonist interaction) with regions listed and follow-up ROI analyses. Thus it meets the fMRI social-task requirement, healthy adult sample, and provides whole-brain task activation results described in the text/tables. No exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition, which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (10 right-handed adults, mean age 26.9), and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self vs other, other vs self) with cluster-corrected thresholding and tables of MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult males (aged 18–35) using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes social processing and decision-making after provocation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (high>low provocation; decision and feedback phases) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction, clearly from the healthy/control sample. Hormonal/genotype groups are reported but healthy-group whole-brain task effects are presented and described. Therefore it meets the fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This empirical fMRI study used a face-localizer task (faces vs objects/textures) that targets social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). It includes a healthy adult sample (n=51, ages 18–42) reported separately from children. Group-level whole-brain task activation maps for adults were computed and reported (mixed-effects FLAME group maps, contrasts such as Face>Object and Face>Texture, with thresholding and figures/tables). Thus the paper provides whole-brain task-evoked results for healthy adults and meets the review's reporting requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses a social-related task (perception/recognition of own vs. others' body parts — perception/understanding of self and others). Sample sizes and recruitment indicate healthy adults. The paper reports group-level voxelwise contrasts used to localize regions (e.g., body minus objects, objects minus body parts, with Talairach coordinates and voxel counts for EBA, V1/2, LOC) and provides coordinate-level whole-brain results in text/tables/figures. Although many analyses use ROI-extracted time courses and ANOVAs, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and coordinates are reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (impression formation about people vs objects) in healthy adults (N=14, ages 18.3–23.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trials) with thresholding (P<0.001) and tables/coordinates for peak activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results are reported for the healthy sample (no clinical group confound). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates.

This is an fMRI study of social group processing in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the main analyses report region-of-interest/atlas-based intersubject correlation results (averaging voxels within 55 Harvard–Oxford regions and ROI analyses for visual/category-selective areas). The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation statistical map for the healthy group (no unmasked voxelwise maps or contrasts are presented); results are reported at the regional/ROI level. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results).

This empirical fMRI study examines neural responses to faces and specifically manipulates changeable aspects of faces (gaze, head view, expression), which are social-communication relevant. Participants are healthy adult observers (n=8). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (Z statistic images, Talairach coordinates, and whole-brain contrasts such as faces vs objects) and tables/figures of the resulting activation maps, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Thus it meets the review’s social-related task definition, includes healthy adult participants, and provides whole-brain task-evoked results (coordinates/figures).

This is an fMRI study using a social-cognitive task (neutral face processing, emotion recognition, affective ToM) in healthy adult participants (N=74), meeting the review’s target population. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task analyses (one-sample t-tests and ANOVA across participants) with whole-brain significance thresholds and results described in text, figures and supplementary tables, not limited to ROI-only findings. Although ROI analyses were also performed, whole-brain task-evoked activations for the healthy/control group are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range ages, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) directly probing social cognition and trust, addressing the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6, range consistent with 18–65) with group-level analyses reported for the healthy sample. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results (group contrasts, interaction effects) with cluster-size correction and provide tables/figures and peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results for the healthy groups (prosocial vs proself) are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 18–58) investigating prosody perception/production and its relation to empathy—clearly a social-communication/affective processing task. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., “happy-neutral”, “question-neutral”) with correction thresholds and cluster reporting; overlap and SVC results and coordinate tables/figures are described. Behavioral correlations with empathy measures are also reported. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (18–55) using an imitation/observation of emotional faces paradigm — a clearly social-related task. The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=28 initial, n=20 analyzed) within the 18–65 range. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain analyses: spatio-temporal PLS voxel maps (bootstrap-ratio thresholded) and a complementary whole-brain GLM in SPM8, with voxelwise results displayed and described. Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (virtual handshake inducing social acceptance vs rejection), directly assessing social processing/mentalizing. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=16, mean age 27.4) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts for the control group (refusal vs acceptance) using AFNI and presents coordinate tables and corrected cluster-level results. Reporting includes tables/figures of the healthy-group activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy task effects, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, a social interaction task probing cooperation/defection (meets social-related construct). The sample consists of 30 healthy adult participants (mean age 21.2), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects and voxelwise) task activation analyses (e.g., contrasts for choice and outcome epochs) with statistical thresholds and figures/tables, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are presented for the healthy participant group (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6).

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (anticipation of touching an animate versus inanimate target), recruiting healthy adult participants aged 21–33, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (paired-sample t-tests and covariate analyses) with FDR-corrected results and coordinates/figures. Resting-state analyses are present but are accompanied by whole-brain task results. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social processing (monitoring others' decisions) in healthy adult participants (N=12, mean age 21). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level SPM analyses with reported statistical maps/coordinates (e.g., peak coordinates and SPM{F} results) and describes correction procedures (small volume correction) for the ACC. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI social task in healthy adults and provides whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (reported in text and figures/tables).

This study used resting-state fMRI (Rs-fMRI) and independent component/connectivity analyses rather than any task-based fMRI paradigm probing social-related processing. The meta-analysis requires task-evoked whole-brain activation maps from healthy adult participants. No task-based healthy-group whole-brain results are reported; only resting-state between-group connectivity comparisons (ASD vs TD). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (resting-state analyses only) and does not satisfy I3 or I5.

The study sample comprises children and adolescents (ages 8–19; mean 14), and no separate healthy adult (18–65) group is recruited or reported. Although it uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (vocal emotion recognition) and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps for the youth sample, it does not satisfy the requirement to include a healthy adult group analyzed separately. Therefore it fails the age-related inclusion requirement and must be excluded.

The study meets several inclusion points (fMRI social task; healthy adult control group present) but does not report an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map or within-group main effect for the control group. The reported whole-brain results are group-by-empathy interaction and between-group differences; no clear voxelwise healthy-control task map (main effect or within-group contrast) is provided in the text. This falls under exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group/interactions reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This study used task-based fMRI (Cyberball social exclusion), includes a healthy adult control group (HC; n=28) reported separately, and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results for the healthy controls (one-way ANOVA main effect of condition in HC) with voxelwise FWE-corrected maps and coordinates/figures. The task probes social exclusion (a social-related construct). Healthy participants are adults (female-only sample) and results for the HC group are clearly described. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social attention (gaze following vs. finger pointing) in healthy adult participants (n=17, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects second-level contrasts and cluster-corrected activations), figures of whole-brain activation patterns and ROI analysis; results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI of a social paradigm (empathy-for-pain) and includes a healthy adult control group, the full text does not clearly report a within-control-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map that is unambiguously identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain analyses appear to focus on alexithymia-based subgroups and group comparisons, and the text describes a between-group contrast (control vs. autism) but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain control-group task effect. Because the review requires at least one clearly reported whole-brain healthy-group task map, this study fails inclusion criterion I5 and therefore must be excluded under E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/subgroup analyses without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

Although this study uses task-based fMRI of a social attribution task (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I4), the imaging results are reported primarily as between-group contrasts (patient vs control) and ROI-extracted % signal changes. The paper does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map or clearly described whole-brain, voxelwise within-group statistical maps for the healthy/control group. This matches exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore it cannot be included for a meta-analysis requiring healthy-group whole-brain maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages ~21) that used a social-related task (judgments of pride, a self-conscious emotion involving theory-of-mind/social cognition) during scanning. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts (pride minus neutral, joy minus neutral, pride minus joy) with coordinate tables and statistical thresholds and regression analyses linking ratings to activations. Whole-brain results are clearly reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (emotion recognition of one’s own vs. unknown child), includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without ELM) with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results (coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics). Specifically, whole-brain within-group effects are reported (e.g., CON mothers show a familiarity effect in the medial frontal gyrus) and whole-brain across-group and per-group contrasts (happy>neutral, own>unknown) are presented. Reporting includes voxelwise, whole-brain results (tables/coordinates and text). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

The study reports an fMRI task (modified Empathic Accuracy Task) that probes perception and understanding of others’ emotions (a social-related construct). The sample consists of a healthy adult group (n=34, ages 20–30) reported separately. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (emotional > neutral, happy > sad, parametric modulation by empathic accuracy, and time-series correlations with continuous ratings) are reported with TFCE/FWE correction and peak coordinates/tables. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6).

This is an fMRI study of social/emotional face processing in healthy adults (N=30, mean age 24.2). The task is social-related (gender identification of angry and happy faces vs neutral shapes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain and ROI analyses are described; main effects of stimulus type and interaction contrasts are reported and supplemented with tables/figures), with results clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are described in text and supplementary tables. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study uses fMRI during social-related tasks (action observation/understanding) and includes a healthy control group, but it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (e.g., HC within-group main effect or HC understand>observe map). The imaging results presented are primarily between-group contrasts (ALS > HC and HC > ALS). According to the review criteria, studies that report only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect must be excluded (E4). Although inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met, the lack of a reported whole-brain healthy-group task map violates I5 and triggers exclusion under E4.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=24, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts and FWE-corrected statistical maps and coordinates (e.g., multimodal > unimodal contrasts, congruency, emotion × modality interaction). Independent localizers and whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (face perception/recognition) with healthy adult participants (ages 19–36). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, cluster correction) and provide Talairach coordinates for significant activations (right precentral and right cingulate gyri), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are reported in text/figures with coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

Although the study includes a healthy adult control group and uses task-based fMRI examining self-related (agency) processing (relevant to social-related constructs), it does not provide a usable whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The authors report ROI analyses showing activation in frontal ROIs for controls, but whole-brain analyses yielded no significant activations and no whole-brain coordinates or maps for the healthy group are reported. Therefore the paper effectively reports only ROI-based results (and between-group ROI contrasts) without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect, failing the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI with healthy control participants and examines socially relevant emotion-word processing, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain results are primarily pooled across all participants or presented as between-group contrasts (controls > ASC) and ROI analyses. Per the review criteria, studies that present only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect must be excluded (E4). Therefore this study is excluded for failing to provide a standalone healthy-group whole-brain task map.

While this is an fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) that includes a healthy adult control group, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. The primary analyses use group ICA across all participants to derive task-correlated components and report combined-sample component maps and between-group (ASD vs control) contrasts. There is no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task effect (control-only map) presented. Therefore it violates the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task map and is excluded.

This peer-reviewed fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (perception and interpretation of others’ emotions via dynamic facial expressions) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~25–26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses and provides coordinates/tables/figures for whole-brain contrasts (dynamic > static, and face conditions > baseline). Results for healthy adult groups are reported separately. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8), using an impression-formation task involving social perception of faces varying in race and socioeconomic status — a social-related construct (perception and understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task analyses (GLM contrast images used for PLS; voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster reporting and coordinates identified via xjview) and presents whole-brain PLS results and clusters. Results for the healthy adult sample are reported directly and are not restricted to a narrow subgroup. Thus the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain task-evoked maps. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (prediction of others' behavior framed as desires vs. rules) in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–44). The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level flexible factorial models, cluster- and voxel-level correction, tables/coordinates and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze processing using a task with virtual characters (social-related processing). The sample is healthy adults (N=30 after exclusions; ages 19–41). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (second-level flexible factorial contrasts; cluster-forming threshold p<0.001 and FWE cluster correction) with reported coordinates and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy participant group. Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity, it additionally provides unmasked whole-brain task activation maps and coordinate tables. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

The paper reports fMRI during clearly social-related tasks (theory of mind ‘Reading the Mind in the Eyes’ and basic emotion tasks) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (n=14). The authors conducted and report group-level, whole-brain regression analyses for each group (controls, patients, siblings) with thresholding and report activated regions as well as MNI coordinates and laterality indices. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are described in the text (and in tables/coordinates), satisfying the requirement for unmasked, group-level task-evoked maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=24, ages 19–31) performing a familiarity judgment for personally familiar, famous, and unfamiliar faces—an explicitly social-related task involving perception/understanding of others and social cognition. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted using SPM5 with cluster-level correction and are reported in tables/figures (activation maps and peak coordinates). Post-scan behavioral measures and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., P1–Cp1, P1–F1, repetition suppression contrasts) are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (self/other understanding in romantic relationships) in healthy adults. Sample: N=42 healthy adults, ages 23–40, within the 18–65 range. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., self>other, positive>neutral) with family-wise error (FWE) correction at the voxel level and cluster thresholds, and presents tables/figures of activation results. The task is explicitly social (affiliation/attachment, perception/understanding of self and others). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of anticipatory interpersonal touch (a clearly social-related task) in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (e.g., Target, Modality, Target×Modality interactions) with cluster-level correction, figures, and a table of coordinates; analyses include conjunctions and voxel-wise results within a tactile localizer mask. Results for the healthy/control group are reported directly (not limited to a subgroup). The study is empirical and not ROI-only, resting-state, or between-group-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria.

While this fMRI study examines social gaze processing and includes a healthy adult control group, it does not provide a clearly identified, unmasked whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group. The reported group results focus on group × gaze-direction interactions and ROI-based small-volume corrected effects within a priori ToM regions; the within-group healthy/control effects are presented in the context of ROI analyses or interactions rather than as an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map. Whole-brain peaks cited for motor/visual networks appear to be from contrasts across subjects and are not clearly reported as a standalone healthy-group whole-brain activation map. Therefore the paper matches exclusion criterion E4 (between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This study used task-based fMRI with a social contingency (pseudo-interactive joke) paradigm and includes a healthy neurotypical adult control group; however, the paper reports only a region-of-interest (ROI) analysis focused on the anterior rostral MPFC and explicitly states that whole-brain and functional connectivity analyses could not be conducted due to signal loss. No group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of emotional (affective) speech comprehension—a social cognitive task involving perception and understanding of others' emotions. It reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with voxelwise SPM analyses and corrected statistical maps and peak coordinates. The sample comprises 51 healthy adults aged 18–53 (within 18–65). Whole-brain results are clearly described and presented (figures, tables, coordinates). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study of emotion processing (a social-cognition-related task) with healthy adult control participants, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The main whole-brain effects are reported across all subjects and the reported results focus on between-group contrasts (siblings vs controls) and ROI analyses. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect).

This is an fMRI study addressing social-related processing (animacy perception and social inference) using task-based functional MRI. The sample comprises 15 healthy adult participants (mean age 26.6), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistical maps and coordinates (tables and figures), and describes thresholding and cluster-level results—meeting the whole-brain reporting criterion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an fMRI study of emotional perspective taking (empathy) using face stimuli—clearly a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults (n=26, ages ~24), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (SELF- and OTHER-task vs high-level baseline) analyzed with random-effects SPM and presents whole-brain thresholded maps and tables of peak coordinates. Results for the healthy control group are reported separately and meet reporting standards (tables/figures and text). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.
