This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines how collective (social) schemas shape memory representations. The task involved participants recalling museum pictures and analysing neural patterns related to collective/social knowledge (dmPFC/vmPFC). The sample consists of 24 healthy adults aged 22–39. The paper reports whole-brain searchlight analyses with group-level correction (TFCE, permutation testing) and presents whole-brain results (Extended Data Fig. 1), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and satisfies the listed inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=51; mean age 22.5) who pass screening for neuropsychiatric conditions, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The task is social-related (passive observation of dynamic facial expressions—social communication/perception of others), meeting the social processing criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects second-level analyses, FWE-corrected p<.05 across the whole brain) and presents coordinates, statistical maps, and detailed methods/results for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; thus fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=37, ages 18–25) that uses a task involving observation and imitation of actions—a social-related process (imitation, perception/understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, group-level random effects, thresholds, tables/figures) and provides coordinates and PPI results. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (social-related fMRI task: imitation/urge to imitate), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (participants aged 19–28) that directly investigates social-related processing (eye-gaze detection, self-propelling motion, and implicit mental inference). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (contrasts such as [E–O]+[S–X], Investigation–Control) using SPM5, with statistical thresholds and figures/tables of activations. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study investigates attractiveness (beauty) comparisons — a social-related task involving perception/understanding of others — using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants. Sample: 25 healthy right-handed British women (mean age 23.5), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (distance effects, conjunctions, main effects) with coordinates, tables, and figures, and describes ROI and whole-brain results. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults. It reports task-based fMRI during multiple social-related tasks (theory of mind, face perception, biological motion, voice perception, language), satisfying I3. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants aged 19–31, meeting I4. The paper presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and mixed-effects group analyses (figures, peak coordinates, and thresholded maps), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not restricted to ROI-only analyses (E2), are not limited to resting-state/connectivity-only analyses (E3), do not report only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within the 18–65 range (E5), and this is empirical fMRI data (E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Animated Triangles Task) with both first-episode schizophrenia patients and a matched healthy control group. The paper reports within-group whole-brain task-evoked activation for the healthy control group (intentional > random movements), uses voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster correction, and describes/control group activations (with individual/group activations in supplementary material). Participants include healthy adults in the target age range (controls aged 18–30). Reporting includes group-level whole-brain maps/contrasts for the healthy group, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (speech act comprehension) in healthy adult participants (n=18 analyzed, ages 18–41). The task is clearly social-related (Social Communication/Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Request > Naming) with FDR-corrected results, tables of cluster coordinates, and whole-brain figures, clearly attributable to the healthy/control group. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This study uses fMRI during a socio-emotional face appraisal task and includes a healthy control group, but the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Most reported whole-brain results appear as main effects across groups or as group contrasts/interactions (e.g., HC > SZ, Drug × Group), and the key healthy-group within-group activation map is not clearly reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses a social task (iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) in healthy adults (ages 18–22), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper reports ROI-based activation analyses and task-based seed/gPPI connectivity within a predefined network and does not present any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group in the main text, figures, or supplement. Therefore it violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain results) and E3 (reports PPI/connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Excluded on that basis.

This study used task-based fMRI with faces (social stimuli) embedded in a target-detection oddball task, reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL mixed-effects, cluster-corrected maps) with figures and coordinate table. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 19.3–47.5). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports a whole-brain fMRI investigation of a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) addressing retaliation/provocation—clearly a social-related process. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=15; mean age 22.33), satisfying the age/sample criterion. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (statistical maps, Talairach coordinates in tables/figures, cluster-corrected thresholds, parametric modulation results), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (Cyberball ball-toss) that manipulated frequency of social interaction and measured enjoyment and brain activation. The sample comprises healthy adults (38 recruited, 31 analyzed; mean age ~21, within 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported (ball-toss [high-frequency – normal-frequency] > button-press [high-frequency – normal-frequency]) with cluster-level FWE correction and peak MNI coordinates (right ventral striatum, precuneus) presented in tables/figures. Expectations/ratings, methods, and analyses are fully described. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete. Confidence 0.95.

This is an fMRI study of social hierarchy processing (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants (three experiments; social and nonsocial groups; ages 19–43; N=24 per social experiment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ‘superior > inferior’, outcome contrasts) with thresholding and tables of coordinates and figures, clearly from the healthy/control samples. Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures and described in the text. The full article includes introduction, methods (participants, tasks, fMRI acquisition and analysis), results, and discussion; supplemental material is not required to meet inclusion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used a social working memory task (SWM) that manipulates social cognitive processing and includes a complementary cognitive WM task, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 21.56) — satisfies the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (conjunctions and contrasts), with cluster tables and figures described in the text, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text.

The provided full text is incomplete (only title/metadata and header information present); core article content (methods, results, figures) is missing. I cannot verify that the study used a social-related task fMRI (I3), that it reports a healthy adult group (18–65) with separable results (I4), or that it reports at least one whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map for the healthy/control group (I5). The title suggests a focus on autism and resting-state/overt interaction, which raises the possibility of resting-state-only or patient-focused analyses, but this cannot be confirmed from the truncated content. Therefore I exclude due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm necessary inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (modified iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I3 — task is social-related (theory-of-mind/social decision-making); I4 — sample consists of healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–38); I5 — paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., COMP>COOP) with cluster-level correction and percent signal change extractions; I6 — whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (conjunction, contrasts, and tables referenced). Study also reports connectivity analyses but not limited to ROI or connectivity-only outputs. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore include in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 21–47) using a social-related task (mental simulation of another person’s actions/feelings — perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (GLM SPM-t maps, ISPS whole-brain synchronization maps, SBPS connectivity matrices) with voxelwise statistics (FDR-corrected) and ROI analyses. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported; I6: whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not out-of-range ages, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study that uses a social-perception task (viewing affiliation vs isolation images while making pleasantness judgments) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects two-sample t-tests, conjunctions, tables/figures). The sample includes a healthy younger adult group (mean age ~20.8), which falls within the 18–65 range, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures and described in the text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content is complete for screening purposes.

This study used fMRI to investigate visual motion processing (moving vs. stationary low-contrast rings) and electrophysiology; the fMRI task is not a social-related task (no fMRI task engaging social communication, perception/understanding of self/others, affiliation/attachment). Although healthy adult control groups are included and reported separately (I4 met), the primary fMRI contrasts and reported whole-brain results pertain to motion perception rather than any social process. The paper therefore does not satisfy I3 (fMRI during a social-related task). I5 (clear whole-brain task map from the healthy/control group) is also not clearly provided for any social task. Because I3 is not met, the study must be excluded from the review focused on social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a well-established social task (Cyberball social exclusion), testing healthy adult university participants, and reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) with coordinates and tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study meets fMRI/social-task criteria and reports whole-brain group-level maps for the control group, it does not satisfy the sample-age requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related: face encoding/social cognition), I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level Dm effects and coordinates for the control group), I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 — the healthy/control group is not an adult-only sample (mean age 18.7, SD 5.8, and the methods state at least 3 control participants were under age 18); no separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup is reported. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered by the reporting format or analyses. Therefore the paper must be excluded from a meta-analysis that requires a healthy adult (18–65) control group reported separately.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI hyperscanning study that uses task-based functional MRI during a social interactive game (pattern game) manipulating cooperation/competition and turn-based vs concurrent interaction, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 44 healthy adult participants (mean age ~22.4), meeting the age and healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (with non-parametric permutation correction), includes whole-brain statistical maps and tables of clusters/coordinates and figures illustrating activation (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked results reported for the healthy group). Thus I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (trustworthiness judgments of faces) in adults and reports within-group whole-brain task activation for the healthy control group. The paper includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=18; mean age 32.2) and reports whole-brain analyses (within-group maps and tables/figures) for controls, satisfying the requirement for healthy-group voxelwise task effects. The full text contains introduction, methods (subjects, task, imaging, ROI and whole-brain analysis), results (within-group whole-brain results and tables/figures) and discussion; it appears complete. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition (Theory of Mind) task (moving-triangles animations) with healthy adult participants (N=20; age range 24–64, mean 45.6), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (ToM > R; ToM > Baseline; R > Baseline) with thresholding and peak coordinates, and a small-volume Bayesian analysis; results are clearly attributed to the healthy/control group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This study uses task fMRI of vocal emotional (social) processing in healthy adults (I3, I4 satisfied). However, the paper reports ROI-based whole-brain parcellation (Power-264) connectivity and graph-theoretical analyses and presents ROI/FC/network-level statistics and figures, not group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or unthresholded whole-brain activation maps. No voxelwise task activation map or coordinate table for whole-brain task effects is reported that could be identified as a healthy-group task activation (I5 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI/parcel-based analyses without whole-brain voxelwise task activation results). Full text appears complete.

Although this study uses task-based fMRI with social stimuli (emotional faces) and reports whole-brain, within-group activation maps for the control group, it does not meet the sample-age requirement. The healthy control group is mixed-age (range 12–23) and includes minors; no separate healthy-adult (age 18–65) subgroup is reported or analyzed separately. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I5 (whole-brain group maps for control group), I6 (acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are directly met. Because I4 is not met, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to CT-targeted affective touch (a social-affiliative stimulus), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=22, ages 19–35). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (arm > baseline, palm > baseline, and arm > palm) with cluster/FDR correction and provides tables/figures of these results, and also reports PPI connectivity analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria while violating no exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI task involving social judgments (approachability from faces), includes a healthy adult control group (n=24) within the 18–65 age range, and presents group-level whole-brain task activation results for the healthy controls (cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates for approachability > gender). Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and coordinates. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not age-outside-range, and not non-empirical).

Exclusion justified because the paper reports only ROI-based task activation results (peaks surviving small-volume correction within a priori ROIs) and seed-based gPPI connectivity and group contrasts without providing an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group. Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: E2 (only ROI analyses reported) and E4 (group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI during a social/attachment-related task – baby-cry paradigm) and I4 (contains a healthy adult control group). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation map reported). Therefore the study does not satisfy the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task results required for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a dynamic social gestures (DSG) task directly probing social versus nonsocial gesture processing (social communication/perception of others). Sample comprises healthy young adults (N=20; mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7) with results reported for the healthy group. Group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported (FLAME, cluster-corrected maps, coordinates in Table 1 and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Although one participant is slightly under 18 (age 16.9), the sample includes adults and results are reported for the healthy group as a whole, so I4 is considered met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses task-based fMRI examining prosocial learning/empathy (I3), reports data from a healthy adult sample (n=31 males, ages 19–32) analyzed and reported for the healthy group (I4), and provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses and results (main effects and contrasts reported with whole-brain FWE and SVC statistics; tables and figures described) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). Results and peak coordinates are presented in the main text and supplemental tables (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not a review), reports whole-brain activation maps rather than only ROI or connectivity-only analyses, reports within-group healthy participant effects (not only between-group contrasts), and participants are within the 18–65 age range. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary references described).

This is a randomized, double-blind fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages within 18–65) that used a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) during BOLD fMRI, satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level ROI analyses and explicitly reports exploratory whole-brain, voxelwise group effects (ToM > gender) for the placebo condition and LPS > placebo contrasts (P < 0.001 uncorrected) and provides tables/figures of these results, meeting I5 and I6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (attribution/understanding of others’ emotions), conducted in healthy adult participants (final N reported: 16–17; age range 21–46), and therefore meets I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial ANOVA, one-sample t-tests, conjunctions) with cluster-forming voxel threshold and cluster-level FWE correction; whole-brain statistical maps and ROI results are described and tabulated, satisfying I5 and I6. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, imaging parameters, preprocessing, and group results) is present. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind and empathy) in a healthy sample. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM activation maps (RFT-corrected) for task contrasts and describes methods, results, and discussion in full text. Participants are healthy college students (age range 17–21, mean 19.3) so the sample includes adults within the required 18–65 range. Therefore the study meets: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants present), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical study used task-based fMRI probing empathy (a social-cognition construct: perception/understanding of others), includes a healthy adult control group (age range 22–47), and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy/control group (one-sample t-test results described and reported in tables/figures). Full article contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: self- and mother-referential tasks and a social attribution (theory-of-mind) task. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=17 analyzed; mean age ~21.5), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (composite t-maps, FDR-corrected results), tables of peak coordinates, and figures clearly describing healthy-group results. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and participants are within the eligible age range. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social cognition (affective ToM, emotion recognition, face processing) meeting I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) reported separately from the BPD patients, meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain activations and single-group results (significance level P<0.001 uncorrected) and indicates single-group results are available in Supplementary Tables S1–S4, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory of mind) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults. The sample includes healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (Experiment 1: N=39, age range 18–60; Experiment 2: N=17, mean age 22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., mentalising > factual; parametric mentalising > parametric factual) with cluster thresholds and a whole-brain corrected map; results are given in Table 1 and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps/contrasts), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining reappraisal of angry faces (a social stimulus) in healthy adults. The sample comprises healthy participants aged 18–57 with results reported for the healthy group separately. The paper reports multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry; Increase vs Observe-angry) with tables and figures of activation peaks and cluster-level inference. Reporting includes whole-brain maps and coordinate tables, satisfying the reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, taskless connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 18–26). The task required explicit emotion evaluation (continuous joystick tracking of emotional valence) versus a pitch control task, which is a social-related process falling under Perception and Understanding of Others (emotion perception). The paper reports group-level whole-brain (surface-based) analyses and conjunctions, with corrected cluster thresholds and detailed contrasts (music vs rest, voice vs rest, emotion vs pitch), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social regulation (hand-holding) that tests social/affiliation processes using a task with threat vs safety cues. Sample are healthy adults (mean age 23.6; n=22) meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FEAT/FLAME cluster-wise maps) with ROIs and coordinates (Table 1) derived from threat-minus-safety contrasts in the healthy sample. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using a task with pictures of social interactions (affective vs cooperative), with 36 healthy adult participants (ages 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric and categorical contrasts) with corrected thresholds and tables/figures, and provides coordinates and maps used to select VOIs. Although the paper also reports effective connectivity (DCM), whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy sample are clearly reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI task explicitly targeting social-related processing (self- and other-evaluation of personality traits), fulfilling the review topic. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) reported separately from the clinical group. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked results for the healthy/control group (one-sample analyses, conjunctions, contrasts) with clusterwise correction and tables of coordinates and figures describing control-group activation. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). The study is not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and does not rely solely on between-group contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using a task (Social Detection Task) that required valence judgments of naturalistic social scenes, meeting the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=38; ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., Social > Non-social contrast) with family-wise error correction and tabulated cluster results, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI during two social-cognitive tasks (emotional perspective-taking and emotion attribution), using a healthy adult sample (n=129, ages 18–35). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level contrasts (e.g., emotional perspective-taking > shape matching; emotion attribution > gender matching) with family-wise error correction to identify task-evoked activations (see methods and Fig. S3) and then report voxelwise regression results and cluster coordinates (MNI) for healthy participants. Whole-brain results are presented in the main text and supplementary figures/tables, satisfying the requirement that group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: dynamic fearful face viewing) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group age 18–65). However, the full text does not clearly present an unambiguous, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain activation (Fig.1, coordinates) appears to be based on all participants combined (TLE + controls) and the paper emphasizes ROI-based percent signal change and between-group contrasts (controls vs. TLE). Because there is no clearly-described unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported, the paper fails I5 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study with healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 28.7) performing social-related tasks (face-viewing with person-judgment localizer and MID). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects parametric whole-brain regression; Table S4, Fig. S1) and coordinates/clusters, with results clearly identified for the healthy/control sample. All required inclusion criteria are met, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, SI referenced).

This paper reports an original fMRI study of impression formation/updating (a social-perception task) in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–45). The paper includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (interaction and contrasts reported with thresholding and cluster criteria; tables/figures reported), and whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/supplementary material. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (False-Belief Localizer; theory-of-mind) and reports behavioral and neural results. The paper includes at least one healthy adult group (Caltech n=18; MIT n=462) with ages spanning 18–69 and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Belief > Photo) for the healthy reference groups, including unthresholded maps and voxelwise analyses. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/figured). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-understanding) in healthy adults using a self-judgment task and thus meets the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages ~21–24) and results for the healthy group are reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects analyses, thresholded contrasts, and tables/coordinates (SPM2 analyses and regression/interaction contrasts), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range ages) apply.

The study reports fMRI data acquired during a social-interaction task (Cyberball) probing social exclusion, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample consisted of healthy adults (n=21, ages 20–37), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper presents group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (within-placebo one-sample t tests and paired comparisons; whole-brain results shown in Tables S3 and S4 and described in the text), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task maps). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of joint action (leading, following, mutual) involving direct haptic social interaction, meeting the review’s domain of social-related processing. Sample: healthy adult dancers (N=18 after exclusion), mean age 40.4, within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with Talairach coordinates and FDR-corrected maps (multiple contrasts, tables, and figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence; results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines moral reasoning—a form of social cognition (perception/understanding of others/self)—using an event-related task, satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=28, ages 18–55) with results reported separately from the ASD group, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy/control group (one-sample analyses pooled moral vs baseline and condition-specific contrasts; FWE-corrected results and tables/figures are described), satisfying I5. Whole-brain results are described in the text and presented in tables/figures (and supplementary material), meeting I6. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical fMRI study tests social cognition (live face-to-face interaction and joint attention), using whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts in healthy adults. Participants were healthy adults (ages 18–29). The paper reports whole-brain analyses (Live vs Recorded; Joint vs Solo Attention) with corrected statistics and coordinates/tables and figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical).

The study used fMRI during a social-related visual perspective-taking task (I3) and included a healthy adult control group (I4). However, task activation analyses were restricted to prefrontal regions-of-interest (ROI) rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper reports ROI-based second-level models and seed-based connectivity analyses (exploratory), but no whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked statistical map is provided. Therefore it fails to meet I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only task analyses). Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity investigation in male children/adolescents (age range 6.5–18.7 years) comparing ASD and typically-developing groups. It does not use a social-related fMRI task or report task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without task activation maps) and E5 (participant sample is outside the healthy adult age range 18–65). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based social fMRI), I4 (no healthy adult participant group aged 18–65), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked map from a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study uses fMRI with a social threat task (threatening facial expressions) and reports a healthy control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the neuroimaging results are reported as region-of-interest (amygdala) parameter estimates and correlations; the paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables for the healthy/control group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (a social incentive delay task with smiling-face feedback) and reports neural activations related to social processing (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=63, ages ~20–36) with analyses reported for the healthy participants (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results and contrasts (e.g., reward > neutral; social > monetary) with whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and coordinate tables (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables). Based on these points, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social tasks (Cyberball social exclusion and subsequent Dictator Game) in healthy adults (N=26; mean age 20.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., Excluders > Includers; exclusion no ball > inclusion ball) with coordinates and tables of clusters and figures, clearly coming from the healthy/control sample. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, tasks, acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), results (behavioral and whole-brain and ROI results), and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This article reports an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~22–23; 25 scanned participants included in fMRI analyses) using a social decision-making task (repeated public good game) that probes social ties/affiliation and understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (parametric modulators, cluster-wise FWE correction, MNI coordinates; activation tables and figures), and describes the methods, results, and discussion in full. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (attribute framing and self/other perspectives), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adults aged 19–41 and is reported separately (healthy group), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., positive minus negative frame, frame-inconsistent minus frame-consistent) with thresholding and peak coordinates described, satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This study uses task fMRI including a social cognition task (meets I3). The sample comprises 493 HCP subjects (healthy adults) and reports analyses on these groups (meets I4). The manuscript references and displays group-level task-evoked activation patterns obtained via GLM (e.g., mean WM evoked activation maps in Fig. 9b and sensitivity results for social cognition in Fig. S4) derived from the HCP healthy cohort, satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content is sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

The study used task-based fMRI to examine responses to face stimuli (natural and bluish faces vs. scrambled images), which addresses social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, social communication). Participants were 25 healthy adults (mean age 25.24), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (natural-colored face vs. natural-colored scrambled image) with reported peaks, figures, and ROI procedures derived from those group maps, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Reporting includes group-level maps/coordinates (figures and table references). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates task-based fMRI for theory of mind (social processing) and resting-state intrinsic connectivity analyses. However, there is no clear report in the provided content of a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. Therefore I cannot verify inclusion criterion I5. Because the reported results emphasize resting-state intrinsic connectivity and the available content lacks a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, this likely meets exclusion E3 (resting-state/seed-based results without a healthy-group whole-brain task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task fMRI of a social construct — theory of mind) and I4 (healthy adult groups reported). Inclusion criterion not met/cannot be confirmed: I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map). Full text incomplete, preventing definitive assessment. Recommend obtaining the full article to confirm task-evoked whole-brain results before including.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self- and other-reflection vs affect labeling), with a healthy adult sample (n=22, mean age 37.4) and clearly presents group-level whole-brain (cortical surface/voxelwise) task activation maps and cluster-corrected results (SR > AL contrast; Figures and Tables). Resting-state analyses are secondary but do not preclude inclusion. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete: the provided content is a website privacy/cookie notice, not the article text. Core article content (introduction, methods, participants, results, discussion) is missing, so I cannot verify key elements. Therefore I cannot confirm that the study: (I3) used fMRI during a social-related task; (I4) included a healthy adult group whose results are reported separately; or (I5/I6) reported whole-brain group-level healthy-control task activation maps (tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the available material. Recommendation: obtain the full article PDF or supplementary materials and re-screen once full text is available.

The full text reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social cognition (mentalizing about friends vs kin) with healthy adult participants (N=25 females, mean age 23.2), meeting age/sample requirements. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and parametric analyses are reported (friend>kin contrast, parametric linear effects across network layers) with cluster-corrected results presented in tables and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Reporting of coordinates, cluster sizes, and thresholding is present. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met.

Full text content provided is incomplete (only title/metadata/navigation/metrics present). I cannot verify core methods, participants, or results. Therefore I cannot confirm that the study meets required inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample aged 18–65 reported separately), I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy/control group), and I6 (acceptable reporting format). No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the available content. Because essential information is missing and inclusion criteria cannot be verified, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

Available full text describes an fMRI social interaction task and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps (figures from 15 participants), satisfying I3 (social fMRI task), I5 (group whole-brain task-evoked map), and I6 (results reported in figures). However the manuscript as provided lacks explicit participant demographic details (no confirmed ages or statement that participants were healthy adults aged 18–65), so I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) is not demonstrably met. Full text appears incomplete for critical participant information. Therefore the study is excluded because not all inclusion criteria are verifiably met (missing I4). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion IDs not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: none explicitly (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study of political attitudes using a modified IAT (faces/names of politicians) that probes social cognition/perception of others. Participants were healthy adults (n=24 analyzed; ages 21–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (congruent vs incongruent, control contrasts), provides voxelwise analyses, tables/figures with coordinates, and uses whole-brain correction procedures (FDR) and ROI-conjunctions — satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-cognition paradigm (EmpaToM) assessing empathy and Theory of Mind, with healthy adult participants (N=178, mean age 40.9, within 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., emotional vs neutral videos; ToM vs non-ToM questions) are reported and activation peaks/coordinates are provided. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social sharing/affiliation) in healthy adults (participants aged 20–33; behavioral n=58, fMRI n=26), satisfying the sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM8 GLM, second-level random effects ANOVA; whole-brain cluster-level correction with AlphaSim and voxelwise thresholds) and lists whole-brain results (exploratory activations like DLPFC and precuneus) and ROI-corrected results; results are presented in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI in a social-evaluation paradigm (meets I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and cluster coordinates (meets I5 and format allowance I6). However, although the sample includes healthy adult participants (ages up to 22.9), the analyses are presented across a mixed-age sample (8–22.9 years) using age predictors rather than reporting a separate healthy adult (18–65) group-level whole-brain activation map or adult-only results. Therefore it does not satisfy I4 (no adult-only healthy-group whole-brain task effect reported). No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 are directly met. Based on the review objective (fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults) the paper must report results for a healthy adult group separately; because it does not, I exclude it.

This is an fMRI task study of social processing (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma; unreciprocated cooperation) in healthy adults (N≈304; ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level task contrasts (CD>CC) and explicitly states whole-brain voxel-wise analyses and presents whole-brain results/figures (e.g., Fig. S2, Online Resources 3–5), as well as ROI analyses. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for a social-related fMRI task in healthy adults and provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked results that can be used for meta-analysis. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present in the provided content.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly investigates social gaze (a social-related process) during a task and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts in healthy adult participants (n=23; ages 21–37). The paper provides complete methods, results, and discussion, including whole-brain voxelwise analyses, thresholding, MNI coordinates, and cluster-level results (not ROI-only and not connectivity-only). Healthy adult results are reported as group-level effects (main effects and interactions). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain results.

Empirical task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation/endorsement of others’ evaluation) in healthy adults (final N=31; ages 19–24). Reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and whole-brain regression analyses with voxelwise p<0.001 and cluster-level FWE p<0.05; results presented in tables and figures. Meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (real-time joint attention task) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 24 healthy participants aged 20–34, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level contrasts (e.g., self > other; JA > NJA) with peak coordinates and cluster statistics derived from whole-brain second-level analyses; results are reported as coordinates and voxelwise statistics (though significance was assessed using small-volume correction within a priori ROIs). These contrasts are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-age healthy adults, is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–31) using a social cognition/joint-attention task probing representation of what another person sees. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and presents whole-brain contrast maps and a table of activation coordinates (place>body and body>place), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: social fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample within 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported; I6: results presented in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study includes an fMRI experiment (Study II) using a social-related task (interactive joint-attention/social gaze), meeting I3. It reports a healthy adult control group (n=16) analyzed separately, meeting I4. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (one-sample t test in controls) and results for control participants are reported (ROIs with SVC and corresponding coordinates/figures in Table S4 and Fig. S4), satisfying I5 and I6 (acceptable reporting via tables/figures). Although many inferential results are reported using ROI small-volume correction, a within-group control contrast (self-initiated JA > NJA) is explicitly presented and linked to coordinates and figures, providing the required healthy-group task-evoked map/peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes healthy adults, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (mentalizing/theory-of-mind processes evoked by Why/How action reasoning), using healthy adult participants (N=17, ages 21–46). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests, cluster-level FWE correction) with whole-brain results and cluster coordinates reported in Supplementary Tables (S3, S4) and surface-rendered maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (causal attribution/mentalizing) in healthy adults. The sample comprised 20 healthy adult participants (ages 18–41) with no psychiatric diagnosis, satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain ANOVA, conjunctions and contrasts; whole-brain results and Table 1) and describes thresholds and FWE-corrected results, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy group are reported directly (no exclusive subgroup or between-group-only contrasts). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion, references, appendix) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (ultimatum game), satisfying social-related task requirement. Participants were healthy adult males (ages 23–28), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (offline whole-brain SVM classification with reported discriminating volumes and MNI coordinates in Table 2 and associated figures), providing voxelwise whole-brain results for the healthy group. Reporting includes tables and figures of coordinates and statistical maps. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study that directly examines social cognition (representation of others’ mental states) using a task-based paradigm (mental state lexical cues and scenario judgments). Participants are healthy adults (N=20; age 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain multivariate and univariate analyses (searchlight and network-level representational similarity analyses) with one-sample random-effects t tests and cluster-corrected maps (figures and tables of regions: Fig. 2–4, Tables S2–S3). Whole-brain results are clearly identified for the healthy/control group and supplemental maps/tables are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (college-aged females) using a social task (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) that probes social cooperation. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., CC vs. other outcomes; context interactions) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates (tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI to probe social processing of gaze (meets I3). It reports whole-brain, group-level within-group contrasts for the typically developing (healthy) group with coordinates and tables (meets I5 and I6). However, the healthy/control group is a mixed adolescent and adult sample (age range 16.1–42.4) and is not reported as a separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup; thus it does not satisfy the requirement of at least one healthy adult group aged 18–65 (I4 not met). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered by the report. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I4.

Although this is an fMRI study using a social theory-of-mind task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) and includes a healthy control group, the paper reports primarily between-group (high-risk vs control) contrasts and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map (or clear within-group whole-brain results) for the healthy/control group alone. This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) probing social cognition (perception/understanding of others) in a sample of healthy adult participants (16 women, mean age 20.8). The manuscript includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotion vs control), with statistical maps/tables and corrected cluster-level inference reported (Tables/Figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data).

Although the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (I3 met) and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (I6 met), it does not report results from a clearly identified healthy/adult control group separately. The sample (ages 18–21) is a mixed sample including participants with current Major Depressive Disorder and healthy participants, but no separate healthy-group whole-brain task activation map or clearly labeled healthy/control group results are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria (I4, I5).

This is an fMRI study using a naturalistic, task-like paradigm (movie viewing) to probe social cognition (DMPFC responses to social interactions). Sample: 34 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.2), satisfying the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation results (whole-brain maps and cluster statistics; Fig. 3 and associated analyses) clearly derived from the healthy participant group. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and empirical fMRI data present).

This study is a resting-state fcMRI investigation in adolescents (ages 11–18) with ASD and matched typically developing adolescents. It does not use a task-based fMRI paradigm (fails I3), and the sample does not include healthy adults aged 18–65 (fails I4). The paper does not report any whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps from a healthy adult/control group (fails I5). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without healthy-group task activation maps) and E5 (participants are outside the 18–65 adult age range). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study using a social cognitive (Theory of Mind) task (animated interacting shapes) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=20; ages 22–56) and reports within-group healthy-subject ToM > random-motion contrasts (tables and figures, corrected whole-brain results). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, healthy-group whole-brain task effect is reported).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (a Social motor response learning task manipulating social inclusion/exclusion) in healthy adults. Sample: 18 healthy adults (mean age 42 ±12) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with FDR whole-brain correction and provides thresholded maps, figures, and tables of activations for the healthy group (one-group t tests). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task results for healthy group), and I6 (results clearly reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (core sections present).

This fMRI study investigated third-party punishment—a social cognition task involving attribution of intentions/beliefs about others (mentalizing). Participants were healthy adults (N=26; mean age 26.0, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects GLM; FDR q<0.05), including coordinates and statistics for right TPJ and right anterior insula activations associated with task effects in the healthy sample. Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity and include unmasked healthy-group task effects. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (social/moral decision-making). It tested healthy adult participants (n=19, mean age 28.2) using an event-related fMRI task probing affiliation/attachment and moral/social evaluation. The paper reports group-level random-effects GLM contrasts with voxelwise results presented as activation maps and coordinate tables (figures and supporting tables), and reports statistical thresholds and cluster criteria. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, Materials and Methods).

This is an fMRI study using a social perception task (passive viewing of point-light biological motion), includes a healthy adult sample (n=48, ages 20–35), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (biological > scrambled motion) and Sex×Condition ANOVAs with cluster-corrected thresholds. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an event-related BOLD fMRI study of self-face recognition, a social-cognitive task (Perception and Understanding of Self). Participants are healthy adults (N=12, mean age 19.36, right-handed males), satisfying the sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., self vs. familiar, familiar vs. unknown, unknown vs. scrambled) with SPM analyses, cluster thresholds, figures, and tables of activations/coordinates attributable to the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) in healthy adults. Sample: N=20 healthy male adults (ages 21–37), meeting the adult age criterion. The study acquired task-based fMRI and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial, whole-brain contrasts thresholded at FWE cluster-corrected p<0.05) with tables/figures of activation maps and peak coordinates. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus, it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of social (human vs computer) interpersonal resource conflict, a clearly social-related task. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Conflict > No Conflict, Human (Conflict > No Conflict) > Computer (Conflict > No Conflict)) with thresholding and tables/figures of activation; coordinate results and whole-brain statistical maps are described and shown. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes adults 18–65). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) using the Why/How and False-Belief tasks, both social-related tasks probing perception/understanding of others. Participants are healthy adults (ages reported within 19–38; samples of N=29, N=10, N=21 across studies), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (Why>How, How>Why, Belief>Photo) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of peak coordinates and thresholded maps described in the text and figures. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a social task (joint attention) in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not present a conventional group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or unmasked GLM contrast for the healthy group. Analyses are based on group ICA component spatial maps and cross-brain coupling metrics rather than voxelwise task activation maps or coordinate-based whole-brain contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (and the acceptable reporting form in I6 is not clearly met). Because the reported results are connectivity/ICA-based without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, exclusion criterion E3 applies. Exclude on that basis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=40) using a social cognition paradigm (viewing dynamic facial emotional expressions), fulfilling the social-related task requirement. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (dynamic > static) with tables/figures and coordinates and a second-level one-sample t-test, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Chinese university students, mean age ~21) that used a social-related task (viewing others in pain; perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (painful vs non-painful contrasts) with FDR correction and provides coordinate tables and figures describing activations (pre- and post-priming whole-brain results). All relevant sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, and the healthy-group whole-brain effects are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task probing social processing (Dynamic Social Gesture task comparing social vs nonsocial gestures) in a sample of healthy participants (mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7) that includes adults within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (TFCE with permutation testing) and presents results in figures/tables (main effects and interactions). The full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, nor non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be included.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none of the explicit exclusion IDs applied. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample comprises healthy adult participants; six healthy adults age 26.7). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (the study did not use an explicit social-related task — participants passively viewed natural movies; although ‘social communication’ is coded as a stimulus category, there was no targeted social task/contrast), I5 (the paper does not report a clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for social processing in the healthy group), and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results for social processing are provided in tables/figures/text as a standard task-activation contrast). Although the study uses fMRI and analyzes presence of social-communication categories within voxelwise encoding models focused on scene-selective ROIs, it primarily reports ROI- and model-based representational analyses rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map for a social-related contrast. Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be excluded.

The study uses task-based fMRI of face processing (perception/understanding of others), which is a social-related construct (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult subgroup (ages 18–37) reported separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (faces>objects) with maps/tables (e.g., Table 3, whole-brain figures) derived from the healthy participant sample (I5,I6). Full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses fMRI during social-related tasks (dynamic emotional face and social attribution tasks) and includes a healthy adult (neurotypical) control group with results reported separately (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain searchlight results are for the combined sample (all participants) and the within-group analyses are ROI-based. Because it fails to provide a healthy-group whole-brain task map as required by I5, it does not meet all inclusion criteria for this review. If a clearly labeled NT whole-brain map (figures, tables, or supplementary) were available, the decision could be revisited.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of emotion perception (facial and prosodic cues) which is a social-cognition/social-communication paradigm (perception/understanding of others). The sample is healthy adults (university students, ages 19–24 in Study 1; 19.67±1.47 in Study 2), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA, whole-brain contrasts, PFWE < 0.05, cluster extent thresholds) with tables and figures listing activated regions and contrasts clearly attributable to the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (audiovisual perception of emotional/social signals) in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 26.6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation analyses (conjunction AV>A and AV>V), voxelwise correlation analyses, coordinates, figures and tables, and details of SPM preprocessing/analysis. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures/text).
