No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical study). Full text is complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study using an interactive social decision-making (modified prisoner’s dilemma) task (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 23–45) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and conjunction analyses for the healthy group (COMP, COOP, RAND > CONT), with tables of coordinates and whole-brain cluster-corrected results (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, and healthy-group whole-brain task maps are provided. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses task-based fMRI with a social/emotional task (facial affect matching), includes a healthy adult comparison group (mean age ~32, n=12), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps/contrasts for the healthy group (Emotion Match > Shape Match) in tables and figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (eye contact and action mimicry), tested in 20 healthy adult participants (mean age 23). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and provides tables/figures of activations. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

The full text contains complete methods, results and discussion for an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 23.6). The task is social (threat to self vs friend vs stranger; hand-holding; familiarity/IOS measures). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (threat minus safe) with conjunction and higher-level whole-brain analyses and reports cluster coordinates/tables and figures. Thus it meets criteria for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults with stated whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly examines social-cognitive processing during personal prayer (a social-related task involving perception/understanding of others/self). Participants are healthy adults (n=20, age 21–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (thresholded whole-brain results, tables of coordinates, and figures) clearly from the healthy participant group. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This fMRI study uses a naturalistic social stimulus and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not provide a clear, unmasked whole-brain task activation map reported specifically for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map presented for the healthy/control group; reported whole-brain maps are either collapsed across groups or are between-group contrasts). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (study reports between-group contrasts and group-collapsed maps without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not report task-evoked whole-brain fMRI results from healthy adults. Although it uses a social-value task (VMST) behaviorally and includes a healthy adult sample (I4 satisfied), the imaging data are structural (T1 VBM) rather than task fMRI. The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI statistical maps for the healthy/control group (I3 and I5 are not met). The authors reference SSC-BOLD responses from a previously published fMRI study in a subgroup (N=29) and use those values in secondary correlations, but this paper itself does not report unmasked, whole-brain fMRI activation maps originating from the current sample. No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E2–E6) are directly triggered. Therefore it fails to meet the core fMRI-related inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This study used task-based fMRI to investigate social-related processing (observing social interactions vs non-social motion) in healthy adults, reporting whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (SI vs NSI) with corrected results and coordinate/cluster tables. Sample: 14 healthy adults (mean age 29.4) satisfies the adult healthy group requirement with results reported for that group. Whole-brain statistical maps and tables are described and thresholded (FDR p<0.05), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting; results are reported in the main text and tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, nor non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED in the review.

The study reports an fMRI face-processing task (neutral face identity discrimination), which is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others) and meets I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (CA; mean age ~31 years, N=17), meeting I4. The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level analyses and displays corrected group activation maps for the healthy control group (figures and supplementary table), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy maps, and participants within age range).

This fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (observation of socio-affective touch) using task-based functional MRI in adults. It includes a neurotypical healthy adult control group (n=21) with results reported separately. Group-level whole-brain task activation results are reported (univariate contrasts and peak coordinates; see text and Additional file 1 Table S2) for the healthy/control group, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion, supplementary references/tables noted) is present and core analyses for the healthy group are clearly described.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: I3 - uses task-based fMRI while participants viewed traffic-awareness videos designed to elicit empathy (social-related processing); I4 - reports a healthy adult sample (20 right-handed male volunteers, ages 20–28); I5 - reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrast (CV > NV) using random-effects analysis with FWE correction and tabulated/figured results; I6 - whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of social touch (a social-related processing task) in healthy adults (40 healthy heterosexual males, mean age 25.8), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation results (multiple whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables are described and reported), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy group are reported clearly and not limited to a subgroup. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplementary materials referenced but not required). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

Only the abstract/fulltext snippet was provided. From the available content the study appears to use task-based fMRI of a social attribution task in healthy young adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the full text needed to verify that at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map from the healthy/control group is reported (I5) is not available here. I cannot confirm whether results are whole-brain voxelwise maps (in text, tables, or figures) versus ROI-only analyses. Therefore I cannot verify all inclusion criteria and must exclude for incomplete reporting. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I5 (whole-brain evidence not verifiable).

This empirical fMRI study used task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self-, mother-, and celebrity-judgments) addressing self/other social cognition (meets I3). The sample comprised healthy adult Chinese college students (17 s/s, 17 l/l included in analyses), ages consistent with 18–65 and reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task analyses (simple and hierarchical regressions), with tables of activations and coordinates and figures describing group-level effects (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not solely connectivity or resting-state, reports within-group whole-brain task effects rather than only between-group contrasts, participants are within the age range, and the paper is empirical. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social group effects on action perception in healthy adults. The methods describe an fMRI action–perception task manipulating minimal in-group vs out-group membership (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy right-handed volunteers (adult sample, ages reported with means in the early 20s), and analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., single-sample t-tests with cluster-level FWE correction) and coordinate tables/figures. Whole-brain results for healthy participants are clearly described (single-video and paired-video contrasts, passive-viewing), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (laughter perception and social information processing) in healthy adults (N=18, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU) with cluster-level FWE correction, coordinates, and tables/figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (acceptable reporting in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are in age range, and it is empirical).

This study is excluded because it reports seed-based/background functional connectivity analyses without presenting a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only seed-based/connectivity/resting analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI data acquired during a social-related task / social perception paradigm) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear report of a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map in the full text). Full text appears complete and methods/results are present, but the paper focuses on intrinsic/background connectivity rather than reporting the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map required by the review.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (viewing point-light dyadic displays depicting social interaction) using a task paradigm; group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts (atypical > typical) are reported with cluster correction and coordinates in Tables 1 and 2 and figures. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=10 males, age 22–32) reported as the studied group. Whole-brain task-evoked maps are clearly described for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social perception/communication (emotional facial expression processing) in humans and monkeys, using event-related fMRI and dynamic face stimuli. It includes a healthy adult human sample (n=23, ages 24–34) reported separately from the animal data. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster-corrected significance maps, contrasts and coordinates) for the human healthy group. Reporting meets acceptable formats (figures, coordinates, text). Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (acceptable reporting) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The provided content is an abstract/summary and lacks the full methods/results needed to verify whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps from a healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related face/gaze task) and I4 (sample consists of healthy adult men). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (cannot confirm the paper reports an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical map for a healthy/control group rather than only between-subgroup contrasts) and I6 (cannot confirm whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the incomplete text (e.g., E4 might apply if only between-group contrasts were reported, but this cannot be determined). Full text is incomplete, preventing definitive inclusion; therefore excluded pending full-text review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related Face Matching Task (perception of others’ emotions/fear) in a sample of healthy adults (N=10, mean age 25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (GLM second-level one-sample t-tests with reported contrasts and thresholds; results referenced in main text and Supplementary Table S2/Figures S1–S3) and ICA group maps derived via GIFT with one-sample t-tests. Thus it provides whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps relevant to social processing. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, seed-only/resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an original fMRI study of prosocial/family-related social processing in healthy young adults (N=25, Mage=20.2). The task is social (family assistance/prosocial decisions), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts and voxelwise results (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward), with tables of coordinates and whole-brain regression analyses, satisfying I5 and I6. Although ROI and PPI analyses are included, whole-brain activation maps and group-level contrasts are clearly reported for the healthy sample. Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (affiliative/attachment scenarios) in healthy adult participants (final N=27; mean age 27.3), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (FWE-corrected, with tables/figures and reported coordinates) clearly from the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of methods and outcomes. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study used fMRI during a social-related task (emotion recognition/gender discrimination of faces) and included a healthy adult control group, but the reported fMRI results are limited to amygdala ROI analyses (statistical correction applied within the amygdala) and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy (TD) group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (direct vs averted gaze), meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=16) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses for the control group (explicit whole-brain analyses and within-group contrasts described; results shown in text, tables and figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, participants are adults).

This study is excluded because it does not include or report a healthy adult group (inclusion criterion I4 not met). The paper reports an fMRI social-related task (PANSIT-MC) in mothers (clinical sample of depressed mothers) so I3 is satisfied. The analyses are whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (own vs. unfamiliar child) reported in tables/figures, so I5 and I6 are satisfied. However, no unmasked whole-brain task map is reported for a healthy/control adult group (I4 missing), and the sample consists solely of clinical participants, so it cannot be used for a meta-analysis of healthy adult social processing. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathic decision-making (social processing) in healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Sample: 32 healthy adult males (mean age 22.8) — meets age/sample criteria. The study reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation analyses (GLM results, conjunctions, tables of activations) with whole-brain cluster correction and tables/figures (vmPFC results also reported with SVC but whole-brain results are present elsewhere). Behavioral and imaging results are clearly described for the healthy group. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 and E4. The paper reports group-level seed-based PPI (psychophysiological interaction) whole-brain connectivity results and ROI analyses (FFA and amygdala), but does not present an unmasked, healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the main face task (e.g., angry>neutral or faces>fixation) in the healthy/control group. Thus it falls under E3 (only seed-based connectivity/ROI results without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (primarily reports interactions/between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: viewing/processing emotional faces) and I4 (sample is healthy adults aged 18–33). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction (gaze-based joint attention) task with volunteers (n=21). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (GLM in SPM5) including voxel-level corrected activations in MPFC, PCC, anterior temporal poles, and fronto-parietal regions for main effects, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are described as healthy volunteers taking part in the task. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a social-related task (charitable donation decision-making engaging empathy and perspective-taking), meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (22 females, ages 19–38), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and corrected statistical maps and coordinates (whole-brain contrasts, SPM results, supplemental tables), meeting I5 and I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates mirror-neuron-related processing during observation of goal-directed hand actions, which is a social-cognition task (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises healthy adult college students separated into alexithymia and non-alexithymia groups (both within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample tests for each group and conjunction analyses) with SPM maps and coordinate tables for the healthy groups (non-ALEX and ALEX). Results are presented as whole-brain corrected maps and ROI-confirmed cluster coordinates. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social evaluation/impression formation (a social-related task) using task-based fMRI (I3). The sample includes a healthy young adult group aged 20–29 reported and analyzed separately, meeting the sample age requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects group analyses, conjunctions, corrected clusters, tables/figures), providing whole-brain healthy-group results (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, not limited to between-group contrasts without healthy-group task maps, and includes adults within 18–65). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=33, ages 18–21) that used a social-related task (viewing social vs. non-social scenes) during task-based fMRI and reported group-level whole-brain random-effects results (social > non-social; FDR-corrected p<0.05) with tables/figures. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion and explicitly reports whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation map), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (recognition of others' action 'vitality forms') using task-based fMRI in healthy adults. Sample: 19 healthy right-handed volunteers ages 21–29 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., how vs what), with thresholding, tables of coordinates, and figures showing activation maps clearly derived from the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI probing self- vs. other-referential and intergroup competitive contexts (social cognition: perception/understanding of self and others), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=21, Mage=23.1), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and provides whole-brain results/tables of coordinates and supplementary whole-brain images (Table 2, whole-brain analyses described), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing/analysis), Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task activations). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation (social-related task) using task-evoked BOLD (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults (N=19, mean age 19.1 years), within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., functional localizer contrast form impression > sequencing with Talairach coordinates, cluster sizes, and cluster-corrected thresholds reported in Table 1; main-task results reported with coordinates in Table 2), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (meets I5 and I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical issues).

This is an fMRI study of social interaction (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adults (12 participants, ages 21–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SPM2 random-effects analyses) with thresholding and tables/figures describing activated regions for the healthy sample. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

Study used task-based fMRI during naturalistic social interaction (live human–human vs human–robot conversation) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (HHI vs HRI and main effects) with appropriate statistical thresholds. Sample consists of 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.8) and meets inclusion criteria. Group statistical maps are shared on NeuroVault and raw data on OpenNeuro. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing full evaluation. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (15 healthy males, age 26.7) that used a social-related task (matching fearful/angry faces — social perception) and reported group-level voxelwise task contrasts analyzed with second-level random-effects models in SPM. The paper presents task-evoked activation results (fearful vs control) for the healthy participants in figures and tables (Fig.1, Table 2) and reports functional connectivity results; although amygdala ROI correction was used for significance testing, group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps/contrasts for the healthy group are reported and displayed. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction recognition (perception/understanding of others) using point-light displays, satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult group (n=16, ages 20–41) reported separately. The authors performed whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SI>NM contrasts) using SPM8, with peak- and cluster-level results and FWE correction reported and illustrated, fulfilling the whole-brain reporting criterion. The full text includes introduction, methods, behavioral and fMRI results, and discussion, so the full article is available. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study includes an fMRI task probing social (social-phobia-related word) processing (I3 met). However, the fMRI results reported in this paper are from a patient subsample (N=25 with SAD) and focus on ROI (bilateral amygdala) analyses and patient-only correlations; no group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map for a healthy/control group is reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results for the task in healthy group). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult fMRI group results reported separately), I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map reported), I6 (not applicable because I5 not met). Exclusion criteria applied: E2.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (valenced self- and other-referential processing; satisfies I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (20 women, ages 18–52), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (e.g., S-N, S-P, O-N, O-P vs fixation and planned contrasts) with tables and figures of voxelwise results and coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

The study should be excluded because it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from the healthy adult group (I5 not met). Although the study uses fMRI in a social/attachment paradigm (mothers viewing own vs unfamiliar infant) and includes a healthy adult sample (I3 and I4 met), its imaging results focus on PET ROI analyses and resting-state/seed-based intrinsic connectivity rather than an unmasked whole-brain task activation map. Therefore exclusion criterion E3 applies (studies reporting only seed-based/resting-state connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text is complete and sufficient to make this determination.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates action observation/execution and mirror-system responses after sensorimotor training, which falls under social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). Sample: 21 healthy right-handed adults, ages within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses in addition to ROI analyses (explicit whole-brain second-level analysis at p<0.001 uncorrected with reported peak coordinates and tables/figures). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind mentalizing task) in healthy adult participants using verbal narratives and behavioral responses, meeting the review’s focus. Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range (Exp.1 mean 28.5; Exp.2 mean 21.25), and results for healthy groups are reported separately. The paper reports task-evoked whole-brain contrasts (e.g., the ToM localizer Belief > Photo contrast, referenced with thresholding and Fig. S1) used to define ROIs and appears to include group-level statistical maps/figures and supplementary material; whole-brain preprocessing and normalization to MNI space are described. Results include group-level voxelwise analyses (localizer) and tests across subjects. The article contains full methods, results, and discussion (full text present). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, resting-state-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map reported), and I6 (acceptable reporting format).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants (healthy adult undergraduates, mean age 20) performed social-related tasks (inferring vegetable preferences and age judgments about photographed social group members) while undergoing fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random effects; main effects and contrasts; coordinates and cluster sizes; figures), clearly from the healthy participant group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Meets I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=21, mean age 24.6) that uses a social cognition task (pairing bodies/names with trait or neutral statements) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (main effects and interactions) with tables/figures. The paper includes whole-brain univariate analyses (Bodies>Names; Traits>Neutral; interaction) and reports coordinate clusters and corrected results, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (co-speech gesture and body orientation) in healthy adult participants (n=37, mean age 25). The task required explicit social-addressment judgments during scanning. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (main effects and interactions) with MNI coordinates and cluster correction, clearly from the healthy sample. Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (supramodal representation of emotions; social communication/perception) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (24 participants, ages 18–34). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM), conjunctions, thresholded statistical maps, and coordinate tables (e.g., Table 2 and multiple whole-brain contrasts), satisfying requirements for reporting whole-brain task activation. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only title/metadata and empty body provided), so I cannot verify whether the study meets inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met / could not be confirmed: I3 (uncertain whether the paper reports fMRI during a social-related task in a way that qualifies), I4 (cannot confirm presence and separate reporting of a healthy adult group aged 18–65), I5 (no verifiable whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy/control group), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results can be confirmed in tables/figures/supplement). Because the full text is missing, I cannot apply the inclusion criteria; per instructions the record is excluded with fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study of self/other social-cognitive processing (conceptual vs agentic self-referential recollection) in healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Participants were healthy adults (N=18, ages 19–29). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (conjunctions and whole-brain FWE-corrected activations are listed in Tables 2 and 3 and described in the text), alongside ROI analyses. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/contrasts), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not out-of-range participants, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (full article content present).

This empirical fMRI study (n=787 healthy adults, ages 22–>35) includes a social cognition task (TOM vs Random) and reports group-level task activation analyses derived from HCP level-2/level-3 group maps (Cohen's d and z maps). The paper presents whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps and overlays/analyses (including visualization and cluster tables), and the social-processing results for the healthy cohort are reported directly. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-task fMRI), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group), and I6 (maps/results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=41; ages 18–24) examining social-cognition and self-related processing during decisions to select and share news articles. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (select>content, share>content, share>select) with family-wise error correction and tables/figures of activations. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for healthy participants), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (perception of third-party social interactions) with an explicit social-related task (I3). The sample is healthy adults (N=14, ages 20–32), meeting the age and sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (surface-based) with peak MNI coordinates, figures, and supplemental maps (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and figures; core content appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (trust/honesty) in healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and neuroimaging methods. Sample: 31 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.3), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (multiple whole-brain univariate contrasts with FWE cluster-correction, searchlight MVPA, and tables/figures describing brain-wide activations), and whole-brain connectivity (PPI) but crucially also whole-brain activation maps/contrasts for healthy participants. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only report; not resting-state/only connectivity; not only between-group contrasts; participants are within age range; paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This article reports an empirical fMRI study of social processing (mental state decoding from the eyes), satisfying the review scope. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task — Reading the Mind in the Eyes), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately: native Japanese and white American participants, ages 18–27), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts are reported, including voxelwise SPM analyses and tables/coordinates), and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text and tables). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, provide healthy-group whole-brain effects, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendix).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (long-term meditators aged 45–62) using a social-affective video task depicting others in distress (social processing/affiliation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative; Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (cyberball) addressing social exclusion/inclusion (I3). The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (20 female HCs, ages matched) analyzed separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (main effects, interaction effects) and reports t-contrasts (noted in the Supplementary Data), and presents whole-brain results and tables of coordinates (I5,I6). The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group task maps) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social attribution (understanding others’ mental states) using a validated social/nonsocial why/how task. Participants are healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–46). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, interaction contrasts) with cluster-level correction and presents whole-brain results in tables/figures, clearly attributable to the healthy participant group. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s fMRI, sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (a social working memory task manipulating number of friends to be ranked on traits), meeting I3. The sample comprises 16 healthy adult participants (mean age 20), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster and voxel thresholds, coordinates (e.g., Table S2), surface renders, and random-effects group inference, meeting I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and imaging analysis details, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical issues). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study using the Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social interaction task) assessing neural responses to cooperative/non-cooperative social interactions—meets social-related task criterion. Sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–22 (both sexes) with results reported separately by sex—meets sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (cluster- and voxel-wise thresholds, whole-brain FWE-corrected results) and applies functional ROIs to cross-sectional data—meets whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core content appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain effects, participants within 18–65, and is empirical).

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and all required inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI with social-related stimuli (own-child vs other-child photos and child behavior videos) assessing perception/understanding of others (I3). The sample consists of adult mothers (healthy adult participants reported as a group; ages implicitly adult and within 18–65) satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, voxel-by-voxel multiple regression) and presents activations in whole-brain contrasts, satisfying I5. Results are reported in figures and tables with coordinates and descriptions in the text, meeting I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are adult, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (emotional crowd and interaction dynamics), clearly addressing social-related processing. Participants: 16 healthy adults aged 19–27, satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects ANOVA results with cluster-level corrections, tables of clusters/peak voxels, and figures—constituting whole-brain task-evoked maps clearly from the healthy group. The analyses are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only approaches. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind/social intention processing including both a healthy control group and a paranoid schizophrenia group. The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the healthy/control group (second-level ANOVA; within-group contrasts and tables/figures of activations and coordinates are provided). Healthy controls are adults (mean age 24.8), and healthy-group results are reported separately from the patient group. The task involves social cognition (private, prospective social, and communicative intentions) and a physical causality control. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related visual processing (sensitivity to spatial relations between bodies; perception/understanding of others). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=20 in fMRI; behavioral participants also adults), ages within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., dyads > single-bodies; facing > nonfacing dyads) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level correction, and presents whole-brain maps and tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; not between-group-only; participants within age range; empirical fMRI data present). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mental-state inference/mentalizing) meeting I3. The imaging sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–22 (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (searchlight representational similarity analysis and repetition-suppression analyses) with corrected statistical maps and peak MNI coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical limitations). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This article reports an fMRI experiment explicitly examining social learning (learning about others’ generosity) and contrasts social vs matched non-social conditions. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=26, ages 19–37). The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-correction and provides tables/figures and peak coordinates for group contrasts (e.g., Gifters > Lotteries, parametric SPE effects). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps clearly from healthy participants), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 25–49) during viewing of emotion-laden movie clips that probe social-emotional processes (sharing others’ emotional states, empathy, perception/understanding of others). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (intersubject correlation maps and GLMs predicting voxelwise ISC by valence/arousal), with statistical correction (FDR) and figures/tables reporting results. Reporting of whole-brain results appears in the main text, figures, and supplemental tables. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of action observation and social cognition: subjects viewed an expert demonstrator making stone tools and performed tasks requiring simulation (Imagine) or evaluation (decide if actor succeeded), targeting perception/understanding of others’ actions and intentions. Participants are healthy, neurotypical adult groups (Naïve, Trained, Expert) with no neurological illness reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 second-level ANOVAs, conjunctions, thresholded maps; coordinates and rendered maps are described), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria appear to be met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, empirical data in adults). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy for human vs robot pain/pleasure) using a task-based paradigm (one-back repetition-suppression), meeting the review objective. Sample comprises healthy adults (final N=26; ages 18–27). The paper reports whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected results and whole-brain maps available) in addition to ROI analyses. Full-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, data availability) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, ages within 18–65). Tasks involve observation and motor imagery of face and upper-limb movements, including meaningful/social gestures (social communication). Reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FWE-corrected SPMs), tables of coordinates, and conjunction/contrast maps clearly from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) in healthy adults (N=23, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction CInt0° > CInt30°) with stereotaxic coordinates, thresholding details, conjunctions, and tables/figures of activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study directly investigates maternal neural responses to infant cry in the context of attachment (a social/affiliation-related construct), using a task-based fMRI paradigm. Participants are adult mothers (mean age 24.1, within 18–65) screened with SCID (no mothers met current MDE at testing), so a healthy adult sample is reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FLAME, whole-brain FDR thresholding) and provides tables/figures of activation clusters for within-group contrasts (own cry > control, own cry > other) and continuous regressions—fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. Results are presented in tables of coordinates and figures and described in text. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processes (charitable giving, empathy, perspective taking; also EmpaToM) in healthy adults (N=33; ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (multiple GLMs, whole-brain searchlight MVPA, random-effects SPM8 analyses with FWE-corrected voxelwise results and coordinate tables/figures) clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 (and reporting is consistent with I6). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults during reading passages that manipulate social content (Social vs Non-social) and vividness, directly addressing social-related processing (I3). The sample consists of 26 healthy adults aged 19–26 (I4). The paper presents group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts (Social>Non-social; Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-level correction and a Table of peak voxels/clusters (I5), and results are clearly described in the main text and figures (I6). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study includes a social cognition (theory-of-mind) task using task fMRI (PPI/BSC analyses) in healthy adult samples from HCP and UCLA (ages within 21–50 and up to >36), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (voxel-wise GLM and activation maps described and shown in figures) for the healthy/control participants. Whole-brain results are presented (figures and text) and satisfy reporting acceptable formats. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text is complete.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment of social cognition (mentalizing about others’ preferences), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=64; ages 18–26), satisfying I4. Analyses used whole-brain random-effects, voxelwise parametric modulation and report peak coordinates, clusters, thresholds, and tables/figures (whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not truncated), so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study that includes a social-processing task (social distance trials comparing friends vs acquaintances), uses healthy adult participants (N=15, ages 20–28), and reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight (MVPA) and RSA results with significant clusters (Tables and figures provided). Whole-brain results are reported and described for the healthy sample; results are shown in maps/tables and corrected for multiple comparisons. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=45, ages 18–34) that investigates neural activity during a social/affective task—generation of cognitive reappraisals for anger-eliciting, interpersonal scenarios (social cognition/empathy/theory-of-mind relevant). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (conjunctions and contrasts) with voxelwise FWE correction and cluster reporting. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (direct and reflected self-appraisals) relevant to perception/understanding of self and social perspective-taking. It includes a healthy adult group (n=12, ages 22.6–30.4) reported separately from adolescents. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses and contrasts (within-group and conjunctions) for adults (e.g., adult You vs. rest; reflected vs. direct), with results described in text, figures, and tables. Thus it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation), and I6 (results reported in standard formats). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper is a narrative review (author manuscript) summarizing prior fMRI studies rather than reporting original empirical whole-brain fMRI results for a healthy adult group. It does not present new group-level voxelwise statistical maps or tables of coordinates from healthy adult participants; instead it describes findings from previous studies. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical review without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria: none fully met. Specifically, I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task) — not satisfied for original data in this paper; I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) — not satisfied as original sample/results are not reported; I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy/control group) — not satisfied; I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results) — not satisfied. Full text appears complete (review article with introduction, methods summary, results discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=25, ages 21–33) that uses a social task (viewing dynamic facial expressions and judging emotion or age), satisfying the review’s social-processing task requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: a whole-brain random-effects contrast (faces > objects) used to define ROIs and whole-brain searchlight analyses with appropriate correction (SnPM), with results reported in figures/tables. Thus it provides clearly identified whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy/control group. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–45) that uses a social-affective task (viewing others’ suffering while applying compassion vs. reappraisal) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain Group × Redistribution Rank interaction and conjunction analyses identifying IPC and DLPFC; corrections and cluster tables referenced). The sample consists of healthy adults and results are reported for these groups. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for task relevance, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (trust decisions based on partners’ pupil changes), conducted in healthy adult participants (ages reported mean ~23.5, range 19.5–32.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, whole-brain maps, cluster-corrected results) with coordinates and figures, and links neural activation to behavior in the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (self-other processing, cooperation vs competition) using event-related task fMRI and reporting whole-brain task-evoked results (family-wise error cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=24; ages 19–31). Whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts are reported in text, figures, and Table 1. The task explicitly probes social constructs (Perception and Understanding of Self and Others; cooperation/competition). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical primary fMRI data). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s social-related task inclusion criterion (I3). While it is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults and reports group-level task contrasts, the paradigm investigates hypnotic suggestion-induced pain (sensory modulation and pain processing) rather than social cognition/processing constructs (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no clear social-related task). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This paper reports task-based fMRI studies of person/biographical knowledge retrieval (a social cognition domain: perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (study 1: n=24, Mage=23.21; study 2: n=26, Mage=20.38), meeting the 18–65 age criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., “all memory > baseline”, status > baseline, trait > baseline) with voxelwise inference (FWE-corrected) and stereotaxic coordinates (Table S6, figures S3), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary references cited).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–27) that uses task-based paradigms engaging social-cognitive processes (Why-How implicates mentalizing/understanding others; CE/Exemplar taps construal relevant to social cognition). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (How>Why, Why>How, Exemplars>Categories, conjunction analyses) with correction procedures and tables/figures of activations (Table 2, Fig.1), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Cyberball social exclusion task (social-related processing: affiliation/belonging). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=20 analyzed; ages ~25), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task-evoked contrasts (social exclusion > fair play; same- vs other-gender contrasts) with voxelwise results, cluster correction, coordinate tables and figures clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (action observation/representation of others’ actions and interactions), tested in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 18–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Observation > Neutral; 2H DIFF > 2H SAME) thresholded at FWE-corrected levels and provides peak MNI coordinates (Table 1) and figures—satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task and analyses are task-evoked (not ROI-only or solely connectivity), and results for the healthy control group are presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of perception/interpretation of others’ actions (social cognition/mentalizing), meeting the review’s social-task requirement. The sample is a healthy adult group (n=12, mean age 27.3 years), satisfying the healthy-adult sample criterion. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (SPM2 random-effects analyses; FDR-corrected maps reported, Tables 1–2 and figures), including main effects of stimulus presentation and regions whose activity correlates with behavioral bias—i.e., whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This fMRI study employed a visual perspective-taking (social-cognitive) task and included a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the authors used a region-of-interest analysis approach with a combined ROI mask and explicitly state that analyzed voxels were restricted to this mask rather than conducting an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Therefore the paper does not provide a whole-brain, unmasked healthy-group task activation map and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study used task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes), fulfilling I3. It includes an age-matched healthy adult control group with results reported separately, fulfilling I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (e.g., mental state > age) with FWE-corrected group Z statistic images and tables/figures, including control-group contrasts (fulfilling I5). Results and maps/coordinates are described in text and tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Confidence is high based on the detailed methods and reported whole-brain control-group effects.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it used fMRI during a social-related task (attributing awareness to a cartoon face); (I4) the sample consists of healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (n=50, ages 18–49); (I5) it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (mixed-effects group results, thresholded and cluster-corrected, with figures and Talairach coordinates); (I6) whole-brain results are reported in figures and tables and described in text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

This is an fMRI study of emotional prosody comprehension (a social communication / perception-of-others task) in healthy adults (n=19, ages 18–51), satisfying the social-related task requirement (I3) and the sample age criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotional vs neutral; complex vs simple) with corrected cluster thresholds and coordinate tables/figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is empirical).

This fMRI study investigates social/attachment processing in healthy adults (I3 satisfied) and reports results for a healthy adult sample (I4 satisfied). However, the neuroimaging results are seed-based resting-state functional connectivity analyses (post-narrative resting-state FC) rather than task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. The paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group (no univariate task-evoked whole-brain contrasts). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based/resting-state connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) and includes a healthy adult control group (18 healthy men), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, although the Methods state that one-sample (within-group) whole-brain analyses were conducted for all five groups, the provided full text does not present or report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map (e.g., whole-brain coordinates, figures, or tables) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The published results focus on between-group ANOVA and post-hoc contrasts and ROI findings (amygdala), without a clearly reported healthy-group whole-brain activation map. Therefore the paper fails to meet I5 and effectively falls under exclusion criterion E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). On that basis I exclude the study.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports resting-state fMRI analyses linking network topology to emotional intelligence and does not present task-evoked whole-brain activation maps from a social-related task. Inclusion I4 is met: the sample includes a healthy adult control group (45 healthy controls). Inclusion I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) and I5 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy/control group) are not met. Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI task study that includes social cognition tasks (theory of mind/emotional state judgments) in healthy adult participants (N=45, mean age 20.5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and random-effects analyses, with peak coordinates in Appendix A and figures showing task>rest and conjunctions. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, healthy adult group reported, empirical whole-brain task results present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices).

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social Trust Game (reciprocity/mentalizing), meeting the social-related task requirement (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (age 18–22) with results reported for the healthy group (I4). The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., defect > reciprocate, regressions), reports MNI coordinates, cluster-corrected thresholds (AlphaSim), and ROI follow-ups—fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and not only between-group contrasts; participants are within the 18–65 range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI experiment of a social-interaction task in healthy adults: participants rated emotional arousal in an interactive (one-to-one) paradigm while undergoing fMRI. It provides full methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported clusterwise FWE-corrected results and tables/figures). Sample consists of healthy adult students (mean age ~24), and results for the healthy group are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 29.4) that used a social-related task (judgments of social concept meaning), directly addressing social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (whole-brain contrasts, conjunction analyses, tables/coordinates, voxelwise thresholds, and ROI follow-ups) clearly identified for the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper issues).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social cognition (stereotypes / knowledge about social groups) using task-based fMRI. Participants were healthy adults (N=19, ages 19–28). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrasts with P<0.05, corrected), presents figures and tables of peak voxels/clusters, and confirms results with region-of-interest analyses — satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI experiment of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others via facial expressions of disgust). Sample includes 27 healthy adults (mean age 27), within the required 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (canonical disgust vs neutral; canonical disgust vs distaste; distaste vs neutral) with thresholding and tables of coordinates. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (collaboration vs. competition) using a task that manipulates social context and measures task-evoked activation during effort production. Sample: 32 healthy adults (ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM, clusterwise FWE correction) with reported statistical maps and tables of activations (e.g., ventral basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (facial emotion recognition) with healthy adult controls reported separately. The paper includes within-group whole-brain task analyses: whole-brain exploratory results are reported for the Asperger group and for the neurotypical (NT) control group (NT oxytocin>placebo clusters are listed and Table 2 provides activated clusters). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes healthy adults aged 18–65). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a social, real-world speed-dating paradigm to probe responses to romantic interest and rejection. The scanned sample consists of healthy adults (age range 19–31; N=38) and participants were screened for psychiatric diagnoses. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8; contrasts, cluster-corrected thresholds) with tables and figures of activations (whole-brain maps and coordinates). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present.

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy for pain; automatic and regulatory components of empathy), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (male, aged 18–40) and reports results for these healthy groups, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (including whole-brain FWE-corrected results, conjunctions, and tables/figures describing activation differences), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplementary material noted but not required), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), task-evoked activation maps are presented (not only connectivity), and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study reports task-based fMRI of emotional speech prosody, a form of social communication, in healthy adult participants (N=22, mean age 24.8). It includes group-level whole-brain task activation results (emotional > neutral prosody; cluster-corrected, reported in Table 2 and figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, task-evoked healthy-group maps.
