The sample and task directly address social-related processing in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and not a non-empirical paper).

This fMRI study investigates social communication (dynamic facial expressions) in healthy adults (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the reported analyses and results are presented primarily as ROI-based/small-volume-corrected findings (Table 2 and text describe ROI/SVC analyses and ROI-constrained conjunctions). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group (no whole-brain contrasts or whole-brain-corrected maps clearly reported), thus failing inclusion criterion I5. Because only ROI analyses are reported with no whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E2 applies. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion provided).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (gaze shifts) in healthy adult participants that reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts. The Methods describe SPM2 whole-brain analyses and report multiple group-level contrasts (e.g., incorrect vs correct; social vs unsocial) with tables of activated loci (Tables 1 and 2) and figures. Participants are healthy adults (behavioral: ages 18–41; fMRI: ages 18–40), satisfying the age/sample inclusion. The paper provides introduction, full methods, results, and discussion in the supplied full text, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of dynamic audio–visual emotion perception (a social-related construct: perception/understanding of others/emotional social communication). Participants are healthy adults (Study 1: N=10, ages 18–33; Study 2: N=5, ages 18–23). The manuscript presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain thresholds noted, conjunctions, tables of coordinates and figures; Study 1 uses random-effects group analysis; Study 2 uses fixed-effects due to small N) and reports peak coordinates and cluster sizes. Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult group maps, empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is included.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (competitive social context) in healthy adults. Sample: healthy adult females aged 18–35 (N=20 analyzed), satisfying age/sample criterion. The study reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (random-effects GLM), condition contrasts (e.g., competition > no competition) with cluster-correction and peak coordinates reported, and figures/tables of activation (mPFC, PCC/precuneus, STS), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an original fMRI study investigating perception of nonverbal social interactions (social communication/perception) using task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=21, ages 23–33). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (multiple contrasts, cluster-corrected, coordinates/tables/figures provided) for the healthy sample. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study with 7 healthy adult participants (ages 20–35) that uses a sentence-reading task which includes many stimuli describing social interactions and people. The authors report voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (factor analysis identifying voxel clusters and group-level factor-related clusters; region locations reported in Supporting Information Table S3) and present group-level results mapping semantic dimensions (including a ‘people and social interactions’ factor) to brain regions. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related processing via sentences involving social content), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines neural responses to social vs. non-social stimuli using task-based fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI with social-related processing: social vs. non-social image appraisal), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 23–50, N=14 analyzed), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrast social > non-social with cluster-level FDR correction and tables/figures), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text, tables, figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations, and conclusion).

This paper reports fMRI during a social communication task (charades) satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=18 analyzed; mean age 27.5), satisfying I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain differential Granger-causality (bbGCM) maps and thresholding procedures (cluster correction) as well as GLM analyses, i.e., whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps attributable to the healthy participant group, satisfying I5 and consistent with I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and materials) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity without task maps, includes healthy adults, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (impression updating), meeting the meta-analysis objective. Sample: healthy adults aged 18–31 (N=21) satisfying I4. Task: social-related impression formation/updating satisfying I3. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (L2>F3 contrast, 2×4 ANOVA, targeted whole-brain contrasts) with corrected cluster thresholds and tables/coordinates and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, and voxel-wise GLM), Results (whole-brain and targeted contrasts, tables/figures), and Discussion — full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, sample within age range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social expectancy violations along warmth and competence). Participants were healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 20.4), satisfying the age/sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses (random-effects), cluster coordinates (Talairach), ROI follow-ups, and figures/tables describing whole-brain results; thus whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps are clearly reported. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample) are met.

This fMRI study examines pain empathy (a social-related task) and reports task-evoked activation in healthy adult controls (age 18–60). The paper provides within-group whole-brain contrasts for the control group (e.g., Self minus Other, Effective minus Not Effective) with thresholding and coordinates reported (Supplementary Table S1 and figures), satisfying requirements for group-level whole-brain task maps. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task maps for healthy/control group), and I6 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-cognitive processing (mentalizing/objectification) in healthy adult participants. Study 2 used task-evoked fMRI (passive viewing of sexualized and clothed targets) targeting perception/understanding of others. Sample: healthy adult males (mean age ~21), within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (voxelwise threshold p<.001 with cluster correction via AlphaSim) and tables/figures of significant clusters (Tables 2–3, Figures 2–4), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related gambling task (playing for self, best friend, antagonist) addressing social processing and reward. Sample consists of 31 healthy adults (age range 18–26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (within-subject ANOVAs) with tables/coordinates and described whole-brain results (with small-volume corrections for a priori regions). Thus it meets the review requirements for task, sample, and whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of social processing (masked fearful/happy eye stimuli) in healthy adult humans (male participants, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates and clusters reported in supplementary tables) in addition to ROI analyses. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examines action imitation/observation—a social cognition task (perception/understanding of others)—in both schizophrenia patients and a healthy control group. Healthy adults (N=16) are included and reported separately. The paper reports within-group task activation results for healthy subjects (e.g., greater activation in posterior superior temporal sulcus, inferior parietal lobe, and inferior frontal gyrus for imitative vs nonimitative action), with peak Talairach coordinates (Table 2) and cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses described in the methods (random-effects one-sample t tests, multiple-comparison correction via Monte Carlo simulation). Thus the study provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group and meets the review objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (racial prejudice/disgust perception) using a passive face-viewing task in healthy adult participants (mean age ~21). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×2 ANOVA, corrected cluster thresholds) with coordinates and tables, plus figures and complementary PPI results. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports an event-related fMRI study of social persuasion (celebrity expertise) — a social-related task probing perception/understanding of others and social influence. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24 young adults, mean age 21.8), meeting the adult age criterion. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (reported thresholds, cluster-correction, tables of activation clusters, Talairach coordinates, and figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

This is an fMRI study of theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults (n=13, ages 22–38). It reports group-level task activation analyses including an exploratory whole-brain contrast (ToM conditions vs. non-ToM) with cluster results and tables of peak coordinates, and subsequent ROI analyses derived from those whole-brain findings. The task is social (cooperation/deception ToM), participants are healthy adults within age range, and whole-brain group-level results are reported (coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical original data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social perception (perception/understanding of others) using point-light displays and human-like walkers while participants judged facing-toward/away — a social-related task. Sample: 16 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.75) within 18–65. Analyses: group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses are reported (ANOVAs within masks, thresholded results, stereotaxic coordinates reported in Table 1), fulfilling whole-brain result reporting requirements. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is provided and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (social preference task) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 23–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Preference > Gender; task vs baseline) with statistical thresholds and tables of activation coordinates (FDR-corrected, cluster extent) and random-effects analyses. Methods, results, and connectivity (PPI) are reported in full. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants made social coordination judgments about ambiguous interactions after tactile priming (meets I3). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=20, ages 23–39) with no neurological/psychiatric history (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrasts (ANOVA and post hoc t-tests) with FDR-corrected results and tables/figures showing whole-brain activations (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present).

The study is excluded because its fMRI analyses are ROI-based (beta extraction from anatomical/functionally defined ROIs) and it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy adult group (exclusion E2). Inclusion-wise the study does use fMRI during a social-related task (I3). However, although the sample includes healthy adults (ages 19–30), results are reported for a mixed sample of adolescents and adults without separate healthy-adult group-level whole-brain results, so inclusion criterion I4 is not satisfied. Additionally, no whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps for the healthy/control group are provided, so I5 is not met. Full text appears complete. Accordingly the study must be excluded.

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: trustworthiness judgments) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–35, with results reported). However, the full text reports ROI-based analyses (mean percent signal change extracted from a priori ROIs) and correlation results; there is no evidence of any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-control task activation map, whole-brain statistical maps, or coordinate tables reported for the healthy group. Therefore it violates E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete. Exclusion rationale: E2; Included criteria met: I3, I4; Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an fMRI task study of self-face recognition, which falls under 'Perception and Understanding of Self' (a social-related construct). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates (e.g., MPFC, PCC, precuneus), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements; results are reported in the text and with coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This fMRI study investigates theory-of-mind/social processing using a task contrasting social (agent-behavior, agent-mental) and non-social stories and reports task-evoked neural activity. Sample: 24 healthy adults (age 18–65) reported separately. The paper presents group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxel-wise thresholds, cluster-wise FWE-corrected results; Tables 2–3) and ROI+MVPA analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From available information, the study uses task-based fMRI of a social decision/control paradigm (meets I3). However, the abstract does not report participant ages (cannot confirm healthy adults within 18–65; I4 not met/uncertain) nor does it clearly report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results for the healthy group (I5 not met/uncertain). No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract alone. Exclude pending full-text retrieval to verify participant ages and presence of whole-brain task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an incidental social task (gender discrimination while viewing emotional faces) addressing perception/understanding of others—satisfying I3. The sample comprises 30 healthy adult volunteers (screened for psychiatric disorders), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (main effects and whole-brain comparisons, coordinates, and supplementary tables/figures) and describes univariate activation maps for the healthy/control group, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, participants are within the adult age range, and it is empirical).

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (watching violent dyadic interactions with attentional focus manipulation) in healthy adult participants (male, mean age 23.6; N=15, N=14 analyzed). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and statistical maps (e.g., all conditions vs baseline; focus on aggressor vs victim) presented in figures/tables and described in the text. Whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate tables are provided; results are for the healthy participant group. The study goes beyond ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate exclusion criteria E2–E6.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study probing social perception (processing of others' pupil changes/eye stimuli), with healthy adult participants (N=14, mean age 22). The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM results, group random-effects analyses, whole-brain thresholds, and coordinate tables/figures) and results are clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and figures reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The full text reports an fMRI social task and includes a healthy adult control group (n=17), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper’s imaging results focus on between-group contrasts (controls > cocaine users) and ROI-based small-volume corrections; no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported (only between-group whole-brain contrasts and SVC results are shown). Thus it fails to provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E4.

The study reports an fMRI experiment directly probing social-related processing (explicit trustworthiness and attractiveness judgments on voices), meeting the review topic. Sample: 44 healthy adults aged 21–60, within the 18–65 range, with results reported for the healthy group. The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunctions, cluster-level FWE correction) and reports coordinates/tables and figures of significant activations. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical article) apply. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This study should be excluded because it does not provide task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation maps from a social-related task in a healthy adult group. Specifically, the paper reports behavioral Theory of Mind (Short Story Task) data collected outside the scanner and resting-state fMRI analyses (seed/ROI functional connectivity and graph-theory global efficiency metrics). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). No inclusion criteria are satisfied: it does not meet I3 (no task-based fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported for healthy participants), and it does not clearly satisfy I4 because participants include adolescents (ages 12–24) and no separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup was reported. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI study of social communicative intentions (prosody), so I3 (fMRI during social-related task) is met. However, key eligibility elements cannot be verified from the abstract: (1) participant sample details and ages are not reported explicitly, so I cannot confirm I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 reported separately); (2) the full paper is needed to verify that at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported (I5). Because these inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the available text, I must exclude the study pending full-text review. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the abstract alone.

This is an empirical fMRI study probing perception/understanding of others’ actions (mirror system) via auditory and visual tasks—fits social-related processing (I3). Participants are healthy adults (sighted and congenitally blind groups; mean ages reported within adult range) satisfying sample criteria (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and corrected statistical maps (cluster-size correction, figures, and Talairach-transformed group analyses), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-age-range, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

The study reports an fMRI task that is explicitly social (face-to-face joint attention game) and examines social-cognitive processing (I3). It includes healthy adult control groups (matched NT and an independent ROI NT group) with ages in the 18–65 range and reports their results separately (I4). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts for the healthy control groups (within-group RJA vs SA and IJA vs SA maps) with coordinates, statistical values, and figures (i.e., unmasked healthy-group task effects), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5, I6). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains healthy-group whole-brain maps, empirical data).

This study uses task-based fMRI of empathy (a social-related task) and includes a healthy control group with adult participants (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (instead reporting group-by-age interaction maps and between-group comparisons). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported). Full text appears complete.

I3 (fMRI social-task) and I4 (healthy adult group present) are satisfied: the study used task-based fMRI examining impact of an adult advisor (a social manipulation) and included a healthy adult group (ages 18–45). However, the paper’s reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps are limited to developmental/age-effect contrasts (e.g., linear age effects, EA>LA>AD) and ROI follow-up analyses; I could not find an unmasked, whole-brain, within-group (healthy adult-only) task activation map or main-effect map clearly reported for the adult group alone. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reporting only between-group/interaction effects without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map) — consequently I6 (acceptable presentation of such healthy-group whole-brain results) is not satisfied in the sense required for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study (three experiments) that directly investigates persuasion using tasks that engage social cognition/mentalizing (perception/understanding of others). Participants are healthy adults (ages ~20–22) reported separately for each study. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (persuasive vs. unpersuasive) analyzed with SPM5 and thresholded at p<.001, with tables/coordinates and conjunction analyses—fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Study 3 also includes ROI analyses but does not replace whole-brain results from Studies 1–3. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study investigates social cognitive processes (theory of mind; judgments of others’ beliefs, emotions, and pain), using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (N=46 females, age 18–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8/SnPM second-level tests) with whole-brain maps, contrasts, and tables described in the text and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Empirical task-based fMRI study of social interaction understanding (cooperative vs. affective), using healthy adult participants (N=27; ages ~24–26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts vs. landscape pictures) with FWE-corrected maps, tables of coordinates, and figures clearly identified as healthy-group task effects. The task probes social perception/understanding of others. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study investigates social-related processing (fan identity, self-referential and social-cognitive aspects, mentalizing) during a task (recall of basketball plays) meeting the review’s social constructs. Participants were healthy adult males (ages ~20–23), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM5; thresholding, tables of activations, figures) for the healthy participant group, and results are reported at group level. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, outside age range, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study examining neural responses to masked emotional faces as a function of attachment avoidance (a social/affiliation-related construct). Sample: 51 healthy adults (mean age 28.5), meeting the healthy adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (emotion vs. neutral contrasts, correlations with attachment avoidance) with tables of coordinates, ROI-corrected thresholds and FDR-corrected whole-brain results. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Hence include for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical dfMRI study of face-to-face eye contact (a social interaction task), conducted in healthy adults (19 pairs; ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM for tasks A and B; paired t-tests for exogenous/endogenous contrasts) with reported cluster tables, MNI coordinates, probabilistic atlas labels, figures (Figs 3–5) and Table 3 listing clusters—satisfying whole-brain reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a multiround trust game (a social interaction task), includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–47), and presents whole-brain group-level task activation maps and voxelwise/statistical results for the healthy control group (figures and whole-brain analyses with PFWE thresholds). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-, other-, and reflected self-evaluations across academic/physical/social domains) meeting the review objective. The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=19; ages 22–31) with results reported for adults separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×4×3 repeated-measures ANOVA; voxel-wise and cluster-extent thresholds with FWE correction) and provides voxel clusters/tables and figures describing healthy-group effects. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This study reports an fMRI task involving social-related processing (naturalistic film scenes eliciting socio-emotional conflict), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=25 analyzed; mean age ~26), meeting I4. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (mixed-effects group-level regressions, voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction) and tables/figures of significant regions, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical fMRI research). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, enabling assessment of criteria. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an emotional face-matching task (social perception of angry/fearful faces), with n=98 healthy adults aged 18–30. The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation analyses (faces > ovals) and explicitly describes exploratory unmasked whole-brain analyses (with referenced Tables S1, S3/S4) as well as ROI and PPI results; whole-brain results are described in the text and supplemental materials, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported (I5), and acceptable reporting format in text/tables/supplement (I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI task study probing social-affiliative/attachment processing (mothers viewing own vs stranger infant videos). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (mothers aged 22–37), with screening for depression/anxiety and excluded participants with high BDI; group sizes and results reported for the healthy groups (synchronous N=13, intrusive N=10; whole-sample N=23). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (own infant > stranger infant) with tables/figures and ROI and functional connectivity analyses. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

The study includes an fMRI experiment (exp. 3) with healthy adult participants (n=21) who performed recall of socially relevant life events (an oral examination involving a social actor) — a social-related task engaging self and social processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results (e.g., hippocampus, retrosplenial cortex, medial prefrontal cortex) with corrected statistics, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition (voice->face), directly addressing social perception/understanding of others. Sample: healthy adult volunteers (n=16, ages 20–31). Analysis: group-level, random-effects voxelwise GLM in SPM with reported group contrasts and peak MNI coordinates; results and statistical maps are described for healthy participants (including behavioral covariate analyses). Although many inferential statistics are reported with ROI-FWE correction, the paper performed whole-brain voxelwise modeling and reports group-level voxel coordinates and contrasts (i.e., group task-evoked activation/connectivity maps). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided material. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study uses task fMRI of cognitive empathy (social processing) and includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–50), so I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper reports whole-brain analyses only as between-group (schizophrenia vs control) differential activation and derives clusters from those between-group contrasts; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or clearly identified within-group/control-group whole-brain statistical map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (judgments about self, friends, and strangers) in healthy adults (n=98, mean age 20.7). The paper reports task-evoked whole-brain group-level contrasts (e.g., self > Bush; friends > strangers) with whole-brain maps and thresholding described, and additionally provides ROI and whole-brain analyses across multiple experiments. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks: self/other, closeness/similarity), I4 (healthy adult participants aged 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical issues). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore, include the study.

This is an fMRI study using a social appraisal (preference for faces) task, including a healthy adult control group and reporting group-level whole-brain task activation maps/contrasts for the control group (figures and tables show PREF>GENDER contrasts and activation maps for each group). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps/contrasts for controls), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic investigator feedback) that probes negative vs positive social evaluation, satisfying the social-processing requirement. Sample consists of healthy adult men (N=21, ages 21–39), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (contrast negative>positive social feedback) with voxelwise and cluster-level correction and tables/figures of activation foci, fulfilling the whole-brain results requirement; coordinates and statistical maps are clearly described. Supplementary monetary trial results are present but modeled as events of non-interest, and healthy-group effects are reported separately. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only effects, out-of-range age, or non-empirical article) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This study meets inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI of social-relevant processing (perception and recognition of faces—Perception/Understanding of Others). (I4) Healthy adult samples are reported (Experiment 1: N=20, mean age ~25). (I5) Group-level whole-brain analysis was performed (higher-level mixed-effects FLAME group patterns were computed in MNI space and used as the basis for MVPA/regression), providing group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps used in analyses. (I6) Results and maps are reported within the main text/figures and ROI regressions. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (study samples: n=41 and n=39; ages 18–24) that investigates self- and social-related processing and their relation to behavior. The paper reports task-evoked fMRI analyses and explicit whole-brain group-level analyses (see whole-brain searches, Fig. S3 and Table S5, with correction procedures described), and results are presented in text, figures, and supplementary tables. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full; the sample is within the eligible age range. Therefore it meets the review’s criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (emotional egocentricity bias) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (random-effects fMRI1 whole-brain exploratory analysis and fMRI2 group analyses with reported coordinates and cluster statistics), with coordinates and tables provided. Sample consists of healthy adult (undergraduate) participants reported separately for each experiment. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (fearful face perception; meets I3). It includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=25) matched on age/IQ (meets I4). The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation maps for the control group, and indicates whole-brain analyses (FLAME) with supplementary whole-brain results/figures and tables for the control group (meets I5 and I6). Although the study also includes a clinical ASD group, healthy-group whole-brain results are clearly reported separately. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study investigated implicit and explicit theory-of-mind (social cognition) using task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related ToM task), I4 (healthy adults, final N=22, mean age 24.4 within 18–65), I5 (reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM for the explicit general-belief localizer with threshold q(FDR)<0.05 and peak Talairach coordinates), and I6 (whole-brain results presented as coordinates/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and reports unmasked group task effects for the healthy sample. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria; fulltext appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an explicit facial emotion identification task (social perception/communication) with both MDD and healthy control groups. The healthy adult control group (n=22, mean age 31.7, SD 14.4) falls within the 18–65 range and is reported separately. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts for the healthy control group (one-sample t tests of the ‘faces minus animals’ contrast; FDR whole-brain correction reported) and provides coordinates/tables and figures describing healthy-group activation. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This study used task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma), enrolled healthy adult participants aged 18–22, and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (e.g., CC vs. CD contrasts across participants and whole-brain analyses thresholded and corrected for multiple comparisons). Results for the placebo and combined healthy groups are described with whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and cluster-level correction. Reporting includes figures/tables and second-level random-effects whole-brain analyses. Therefore it satisfies the review’s fMRI/social-task, healthy adult sample, whole-brain evidence, and acceptable reporting format criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary materials are referenced but not required for inclusion.

This is an fMRI hyperscanning study using a social joint-attention task (meets I3). The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult group (80 healthy controls, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately from clinical groups (meets I4). The authors conducted whole-brain task analyses (INT > NoINT) and entered HC-HC [INT>NoINT] contrast images into group-level ANOVAs, reporting whole-brain analyses and testing HC versus BPD groups; therefore at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy/control group is present in the reported analyses (meets I5). Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/supplemental procedures are referenced (meets I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered based on the provided content.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (cooperation vs competition) using a task involving others (meets social-related processing). Participants: 12 healthy adults aged 21–28 (meets healthy adult sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (cooperation vs independent, competition vs independent, direct contrasts) with voxelwise thresholding and tables/figures of activations (coordinates reported). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task addressing Perception and Understanding of Self). It enrolled 12 healthy adult participants (mean age 19.36), meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts (e.g., self vs. familiar, familiar vs. unknown) and presents thresholding and cluster results (tables/figures of activation), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, empirical healthy-group task activations reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an original fMRI study using a social-related task (judging meaning relatedness of social concepts) in healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 29.4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain categorical contrasts and conjunction analyses) with coordinates and figures, and results for the healthy sample are clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This empirical study uses task-based BOLD fMRI during social cognition (theory-of-mind) tasks involving cooperation and deception in cartoons, reporting group-level results. Participants are healthy adults (n=13, ages 22–38), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports exploratory whole-brain random-effects analyses and direct contrasts (paired t-tests) comparing ToM conditions to a non-ToM control and between conditions, with tables of peak coordinates, figures, and statistical thresholds—providing whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps/results for the healthy group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines neural processing of social hierarchy (a social cognitive task), meeting the review objective. Participants: healthy adults (n=72 across experiments; ages within 19–43), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and thresholded statistical maps/coordinate tables for contrasts of interest (e.g., ‘superior > inferior’, outcome contrasts) clearly identified as healthy/control group effects. Results are presented in figures and tables. Full article core content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range samples, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-referential, mother-referential, and social attribution tasks) in healthy adult participants (n=17 analyzed, mean age 21.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Self vs. Letter, Mother vs. Letter, Friends vs. Bumper Cars) with statistical maps and tables of coordinates (Tables 2–5) and uses FDR correction for multiple comparisons. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing full assessment.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (a social motor response/inclusion–exclusion task) in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 42±12), satisfying the sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (one-group t tests) with results described and thresholded using FDR whole-brain correction and displayed in figures/tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The social task directly probes social-related constructs (social inclusion/exclusion, affiliation/communication), meeting the task inclusion. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 20) using tasks that invoke perception and understanding of others (inferring preferences vs categorical age judgments), meeting I3 and I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts, Talairach coordinates, cluster sizes, figures and tables of activations (mPFC and other regions), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (gaze-based social interaction task) in healthy adults. The sample includes healthy participants aged 18–40 (N=12) satisfying the adult age range. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses using SPM2, with multiple contrasts (e.g., gaze-shift minus no-movement; incorrect vs correct; social vs unsocial) and tabulated loci (Tables 1–2) and figures, meeting the requirement for whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (behavioural and fMRI procedures, subjects, imaging, analysis), Results, and Discussion; thus full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that included social stimuli (face targets) embedded in a target-detection task (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adults (N=19; ages 19.3–47.5) screened for psychiatric symptoms (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (shape targets vs novels; face targets vs novels; and direct contrasts) analyzed with FSL mixed-effects and cluster correction and provides figures and MNI coordinates (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI experiment probing social-related processing (monitoring others' pupils) in healthy adults. Methods include whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses with reported voxelwise results (main effects and interactions) and coordinates/figures. Sample: 14 healthy right-handed adults (mean age 22), within 18–65. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures reported). No exclusion criteria appear to be met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of self-related social processing (perception/understanding of self), using a task (general vs contextual self judgments) — meets I3. Participants are healthy adults (university students ages reported within 18–65) — meets I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level task contrasts and regression analyses with tables and coordinates and thresholding described — meets I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion so is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using the Reading the Mind in the Eyes task—a social-perceptual/mentalizing task—on healthy adult participants (native Japanese and white American, ages 18–27). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation contrasts and tables of regions/coordinates (multiple tables, group contrasts, and thresholding information), clearly reporting healthy-group task effects. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (Trust Game) probing reciprocity and perspective-taking, conducted in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., defect > reciprocate; regressions with reciprocity) with stereotactic coordinates and tables/figures, and describes whole-brain preprocessing and statistical inference (SPM2, AlphaSim correction). Whole article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI social processing study in healthy adults and provides whole-brain healthy-group results. No exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an fMRI task probing attachment/affiliation (masked facial emotion) in a sample of 51 healthy adults (mean age 28.5), satisfying the social-processing and healthy adult sample criteria. The report includes whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (main effects of masked sad/happy faces vs neutral, and regressions with attachment scores) with coordinates and corrected thresholds, clearly pertaining to the healthy group. Results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore this study meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates direct and reflected self-appraisals (a social-cognition/self-perception task). It includes a healthy adult group (N=12, ages 22.6–30.4) reported separately from adolescents. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (unmasked, corrected for multiple comparisons) with tables/coordinates and detailed methods and results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes healthy adult whole-brain task activations).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (joint attention / attribution of what another sees) in healthy adults (ages 20–31). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and contrasts (body>place and place>body), with figures and a table of activation coordinates, clearly from the healthy participant sample. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (a social decision task) in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results. It meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — charitable giving), I4 (healthy adult sample, N=22, ages 19–38), I5 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts with corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text and supplemental tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports task-based fMRI during live social interaction and a joint-attention task in healthy adults (ages 18–29). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., Live > Recorded; Joint Attention > Solo Attention) with corrected statistics and coordinate tables and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The methods, results, and discussion are present, and healthy control group results are reported separately. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (social expectancy violations along warmth and competence) using a task with pictures and attributions, conducted in healthy adult participants (final N=12, mean age 20.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates, cluster thresholds, and corrected significance (p<.001) and tables/figures of activations. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study investigates social preference (a social-related task) in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts. Sample: 21 healthy adults, ages 23–51 (within 18–65). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (Preference > Gender contrast) with tables of coordinates, figures, and FDR-corrected thresholds, clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample issues). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (mentalizing/perception of others) using images of sexualized and clothed targets, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample includes healthy adult participants (heterosexual men, n=21, mean age ~21), meeting the age/sample criterion for healthy adults. The manuscript reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (voxelwise threshold p<.001, AlphaSim cluster correction) and presents cluster tables and figures, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are reported (within-group contrasts and correlations with hostile sexism). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/ connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical work) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports original fMRI data on a social communication task (charades) with healthy adult participants (mean age 27.5; final N=18), and includes group-level whole-brain analyses (GLM and Granger-causality whole-brain maps) identifying task-evoked effects. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including participants, task, GLM and whole-brain Granger-causality analyses), Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study used fMRI during a social-related task (dynamic facial expression perception) in a healthy adult sample (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the reported statistical results focus on ROI analyses with small-volume correction (amygdala, insula, striatum, OFC) and conjunctions within these ROIs. The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group; results are reported via ROI SVC and ROI-based contrasts. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete. Exclusion summary: E2 met; Inclusion met: I3, I4; Inclusion not met: I5.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/inferring others’ preferences), using task-based functional MRI with healthy adult participants (n=64; ages 18–26). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses linking self–other discrepancy to BOLD response in MPFC and other regions, with peak coordinates and tables described. The design, methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text, and whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (gaze-mediated social vs nonsocial stimuli) in healthy adults. Methods and results include whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (first- and second-level GLM in SPM5), cluster-level corrected SPMs, and tables/figures reporting activation coordinates and contrasts (main effects and interactions). Sample: 23 healthy right-handed adults aged 21–37. The paper reports task-evoked, unmasked whole-brain healthy-group contrasts (e.g., INC>CON, SOC>OBJ, interaction INC×SOC). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, participant ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria satisfied: none.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (judgments about self, friends, and strangers) in healthy adults (N=98; mean age 20.7), satisfying the review’s focus on social-related processing. The full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., self > other; friends > strangers) with thresholded whole-brain maps and ROI analyses, and these are clearly identified as healthy-group effects. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 24.8) that investigates face processing (perception/understanding of others), a social-cognition construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA, voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction) and describes whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures (Supplementary Table S1 and Figure S1). The healthy adult group results are reported clearly and are suitable for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using a social-related task (observing point-light social interactions vs non-social movements). Sample: 14 healthy adults (mean age 29.4) within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrast (SI vs NSI) with FDR-corrected results, tables of peak coordinates, and figures — satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of prosocial decisions (social-related processing) in healthy young adults (Mage=20.2), meeting the topic and sample criteria. The paper reports group-level task-evoked whole-brain contrasts (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and whole-brain analyses, and also reports PPI connectivity; results are clearly described for the healthy participant sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-related task under 'Perception and Understanding of Self'), using healthy adult participants (final fMRI sample N=16, ages 19–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (SPM) with reported coordinates and cluster-level correction (P < 0.05, FWE cluster-corrected) for task contrasts (e.g., Morph 50% self vs friend; Morph 100% vs 60%), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during observation of virtual social interactions (meets I3). Methods describe recruitment of healthy consenting subjects and results are based on 15 participants, consistent with a healthy adult sample (I4) though exact ages are not explicitly listed in the provided text. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain activation maps and t-value maps for social interaction vs. control contrasts (figures and text describing whole-brain activations), satisfying I5 and I6. Full text includes methods, scanning parameters, preprocessing, and representative results, so fulltext is treated as complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met based on provided content.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (eye contact and mimicry) using task-based whole-brain GLM analyses and DCM. Participants: 20 healthy adults (mean age 23) meeting adult age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Congruent > Catch, Direct-Cong > Averted-Cong, interaction contrasts) with thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction; results are presented in Table 1 and Figures, indicating whole-brain healthy-group task effects. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly probes social cognition (stereotypes/social-category knowledge) using task-based fMRI. The sample is healthy adults (N=19, ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., ‘social > non-social’ and ‘non-social > social’) with correction (P < 0.05) and provides tables/figures of peak voxels and clusters. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain healthy adult fMRI studies of social processing.

This is an fMRI study of emotional (social) perception/integration using a task requiring audiovisual emotion classification—clearly a social-related construct (I3). Sample comprises 24 healthy adults aged 18–34, within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (RFX-GLM) with conjunctions and corrected thresholds and presents whole-brain activation tables/figures (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range samples, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses task-based fMRI (Cyberball) probing social exclusion, a social-related process (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adults 18–65 (n=20 after exclusions), reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts with statistical thresholds, cluster correction, tables/figures of coordinates and maps (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: whole-brain results are present (E2/E3/E4 not met), participants are within age range (E5 not met), and this is empirical fMRI data (E6 not met). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the ultimatum game (a social interaction task) in healthy adult participants (male, ages 23–28). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported in the offline classification (discriminating volumes with MNI coordinates and thresholded p-values; Table 2 and figures), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-related results reported for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-affective (CT-targeted) touch in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–35) and directly addresses social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain RFX GLM task contrasts (arm>baseline, palm>baseline, arm>pal m) with thresholding and tables/figures of voxelwise results and also describes PPI connectivity. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of emotional prosody comprehension, a social-communication task probing perception/understanding of others’ emotions. Participants were healthy adults (N=19 males, ages 18–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., emotional vs neutral, complex vs simple) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tables of local maxima; analyses and results are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults investigating social processing (team membership/in-group bias) using task-based fMRI. It reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrasts (e.g., action videos vs fixation; decision vs press) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The sample comprises healthy adult volunteers (age range reported 17–43; the sample includes adults within 18–65 and results are reported for the healthy group), and analyses include second-level random-effects group maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, not outside age range exclusively, and not non-empirical). Note: a small number of participants were age 17, but the study nonetheless includes and reports analyses on healthy adult participants, so I4 is considered satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (a social working memory task) with healthy adult participants (N=16; mean age 20). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric effects across load), provides coordinates and figures, and describes whole-brain statistical thresholds and cluster correction. Behavioral task, methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables and clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of empathic decision-making (social cognition/understanding of others), using a task where subjects made purchase decisions for another person — clearly a social-related task. Sample: 32 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.8), meeting the 18–65 healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLMs) with whole-brain cluster-corrected inference and tables of activations; conjunctions and contrasts are reported for the healthy group. Whole-brain results are described in text/tables and figures (with cluster-corrected thresholds), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study that measured neural responses while participants judged pleasantness of images depicting social affiliation and isolation (I3). The sample includes a younger healthy adult group (N=16; mean age 20.75), which falls within the required 18–65 range, satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses (random-effects SPM analyses) with tables of coordinates and figures, meeting the whole-brain reporting requirement (I5, I6). It is not limited to ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical work, and the provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self- vs other-referential processing) in healthy adults, using a task that manipulates self/other and valence. Sample: 20 healthy adult women aged 18–52 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked BOLD results with figures and tables of voxelwise activations and contrasts (e.g., S-N, S-P vs fixation and vs other conditions), and reports ROI and whole-brain cluster statistics. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of social evaluation/impression formation (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy young adult group aged 20–29 (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts and conjunction analyses (social vs non-social; social-meaningful vs social-irrelevant) with cluster correction and tables/figures, clearly identifying activations for the age groups including the young healthy group (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group whole-brain effects (so E2–E4 not met), and the study is empirical with original fMRI data (E6 not met). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study is an fMRI investigation of social cognition (impression formation/updating of others), using task-based BOLD in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (interaction and L2>F3 contrasts), with thresholding, tables/figures, and coordinates described in the text and supplements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (threat to self, friend, stranger) using task-based fMRI and analyses directly addressing self/other processing (meets I3). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=22, mean age 23.6), meeting the age/sample requirement (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (non-masked conjunction analyses, whole-brain corrected analyses, and whole-brain contrasts) with results presented in figures/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not a between-group-only contrast, participant ages are within range, and it is an empirical report with original fMRI data. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social influence (expert advice) on decision-making that includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation results with cluster-corrected coordinates. The task is explicitly social (advice from an adult expert) and examines social-cognition regions (TPJ) and valuation/control networks, satisfying the review’s focus on social-related processing. Whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates are reported and described in the text and supplementary material. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, non-empirical, or adult-age exclusion) are met.
