This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16, ages 25–49) that used task-based movie viewing with social/emotional content relevant to perception/understanding of others (meets I3 and I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain intersubject-correlation (ISC) maps and valence-/arousal-by-ISC GLM results with voxelwise permutation testing and FDR correction, and seed-voxel correlation whole-brain network maps (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=27, ages ~25) that used task-based functional MRI during observation of social interactions (cooperative vs affective), addressing social cognition/perception of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, whole-brain contrasts, FWE-corrected maps) with tables and figures of activation foci, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–34) using a social-related task (viewing movie clips annotated for eight social features) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation analyses (first- and second-level GLM, one-sample t-tests, FDR-corrected maps; coordinates and figures provided). The sample falls within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain results are clearly described and presented. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures, and discussion present). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of affiliative social scenarios in healthy adults. The paper reports a behavioral paradigm and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected results and contrasts), with ROI and whole-brain results presented in tables/figures. Sample: healthy adults (final N=27; ages within 18–65). The affiliative task clearly maps onto social-related processing (affiliation/attachment). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and it is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of criteria.

All inclusion criteria are met: (I3) the task is social-related (maternal attachment/response to infant cry) during fMRI; (I4) participants are adult mothers (mean age 24.1, within 18–65) and results are reported for this adult group; (I5) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FSL, whole-brain FDR thresholding, cluster coordinates); (I6) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text (MNI coordinates provided). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and participants are within the age range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (social texts and social videos probing theory-of-mind, emotion and moral reasoning), uses a healthy adult sample (n=45, mean age 20.5, ages 19–23), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (strict conjunction, random- and fixed-effects results) with peak coordinates in Appendix A and figures showing statistical maps. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and supplementary stimulus material; core content is present, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates processing of emotional facial expressions (a social communication task) in healthy adult humans. The sample includes 23 healthy adult participants aged 24–34 (meets I4). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and significance thresholds (random-effects group analysis, cluster-correction) with figures and coordinate tables (meets I5 and I6). The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others’ emotions; meets I3). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=21, ages within 18–65) investigating action observation/execution and mirror-system responses—relevant to social cognition (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, task-evoked whole-brain analyses (a whole-brain second analysis at p<0.001 uncorrected) and provides peak coordinates and tables/figures of results. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition using a task manipulating ostensive vs. non-ostensive cues (meets I3). Sample: 22 healthy adults (mean age 25) with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). Authors report group-level, whole-brain RFX analyses (Three-Way repeated measures whole-brain ANOVA) and note exploratory whole-brain findings (early visual/V1), indicating at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task effect (meets I5). Results are reported in the main text and tables/figures (acceptable per I6). Although many reported effects are ROI small-volume corrected, whole-brain analyses were conducted and reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/perception of others’ pain). It used task-based fMRI during a social-related task (viewing others in pain), recruited healthy adult participants (n≈36, mean age ~21), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (painful vs non-painful) with FDR-corrected results and tables/figures. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group task map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5) using a social resource-conflict task (human vs computer opponent), directly addressing social processing. Group-level, whole-brain task contrasts are reported (e.g., Conflict > No-Conflict; interaction [Human (Conflict > No Conflict)] > [Computer (Conflict > No Conflict)]) with thresholding and tables/figures describing results. Behavioral and covariate whole-brain regression analyses are also reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–27) that examines social-cognition–relevant processes (why/how action identification and category/exemplar generation; discussion links to mentalizing/theory-of-mind). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (one-sample t-tests in SPM5) with corrected thresholds and region tables/figures for the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, age is within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

The paper reports an empirical fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (25 right-handed British women, mean age 23.5) who performed social-related judgments (beauty/attractiveness comparisons of people) during task fMRI. The manuscript provides group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (whole-brain contrasts, conjunctions, and coordinate tables/figures) and ROI checks; results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinates. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (scanned N=38, ages 19–31) using a social task (speed-dating paradigm) that probes affiliation/attachment and perception of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts with thresholding and tables of MNI coordinates (multiple contrasts: main effect of partner decision, violations of expectations, RL-based prediction errors, Match>Unrequited, etc.). Results are presented as whole-brain maps/tables and described for the healthy/control group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) using a task-based paradigm (meets I3). Sample comprises 23 healthy adult participants (mean age 24), within 18–65 years (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and peak coordinates (e.g., CInt > PInt, interaction effects) with voxelwise thresholds and tables/figures, and reports PPI connectivity additionally — thus whole-brain task activations are available (meets I5 and I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so completeness is adequate. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy groups, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social regulation (hand-holding with friend/stranger/alone) in healthy adults (mean age ~23.6), addressing social/affiliation processes. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FLAME, cluster-wise Z>2.3, cluster p<.05), lists ROIs and presents whole-brain effects in the Results and Table 1. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults investigating social communication (perception of different laughter types) with explicit and implicit social-processing tasks. The sample comprises 18 healthy adults (mean age 26) and participants’ data are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (contrasts, cluster- and FWE-corrected results) and provides tables/figures of whole-brain results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked fMRI in healthy adults addressing social-related processing.

This study reports task-based fMRI using images of human suffering while participants applied compassion or reappraisal (a social-related task targeting perception/understanding of others). The sample consists of healthy adults (ages 18–45) with group-level analyses reported. The paper presents whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (Group × Redistribution Rank interaction and conjunction/PPI whole-brain/ROI-corrected analyses) with tables/figures referenced in the main and supplemental materials. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed a gambling task involving outcomes for self, best friend, and an experimentally created ‘antagonist’, addressing social relationship effects on neural reward processing. Sample: 31 healthy adults (mean age 20.9, range 18–26) meets the adult (18–65) healthy-group requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (within-subject ANOVAs at trial onset and outcome), with coordinates, tables, and figures; small-volume corrections were applied for a priori ROIs but whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables are presented. Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures satisfies acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This empirical fMRI study assessed social perception (recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’) using a task in which healthy adult participants (N=19; ages 21–29) viewed and judged interactions between actors. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8 random-effects, contrasts such as how vs what with PFWE thresholds, tables of coordinates and rendered maps) clearly identified for the healthy participant group. All required inclusion criteria are met (fMRI social-related task; healthy adult sample within 18–65; whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported; acceptable formats of results). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=46, ages 18–31) investigating theory-of-mind/emotion/pain judgments — clearly social-related processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (univariate second-level maps, MVPA results) with figures/tables and thresholding procedures, satisfying whole-brain evidence. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports an fMRI task that manipulates social evaluation (a peer-watching paradigm), satisfying I3 (social-related task). The sample includes healthy adult participants aged 18.0–22.9 within the reported sample, satisfying I4. The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group analyses and presents corrected whole-brain results (e.g., MPFC cluster coordinates and corrected p-values), satisfying I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps). Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures meets I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced but its absence is acceptable, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and healthy adult data are present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is included.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (nonverbal dyadic interactions) with a task in which healthy adult participants (n=21; ages 23–33) performed ratings during scanning, fulfilling the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (multiple contrasts such as contingent>mirrored, rigid>smooth, and comparisons to scrambled baseline) with cluster-level correction, MNI coordinates, and tables of activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and whole-brain fMRI results), and Discussion, so core article content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) apply. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an fMRI study of social impression formation in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 19.1), meeting the population criterion. The experiment used task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (impression-formation main task and a validated impression-formation functional localizer), satisfying the social-processing requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast results from the functional localizer (form impression > sequencing) with cluster-corrected activations and Talairach coordinates (Tables/Results), which fulfills the requirement for at least one healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Results for the main task are analyzed within an a priori localizer-defined ROI but the presence of the whole-brain localizer map ensures I5 is met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social perception (biological motion) involving healthy adult participants (n=48, ages 20–35) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (main effect Biological>Scrambled, Sex×Condition ANOVA) with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activation coordinates. The adult healthy group results are reported separately from child/adolescent data. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (ages 19–28) using tasks probing perception of others (eye-gaze, self-propelling motion, and implicit mental inference). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5; voxel-by-voxel regression, cluster correction) and provides coordinates, statistical thresholds, and activation maps/tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This fMRI study investigates third-party punishment (a social cognition task involving attribution of intentions and moral responsibility) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants. It reports methods, results, and interpretation in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding (q(FDR)<0.05) and reported Talairach coordinates. Sample: 26 healthy adults (age mean 26, right-handed) within 18–65. Whole-brain activation maps and coordinates are reported for main effects and interactions (R TPJ, R anterior insula). Therefore it satisfies I3 (task-based social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (coordinates/figures/text reporting). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical with healthy adults). Full text appears complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI of face perception (a social-related process) and includes a healthy adult participant group reported separately, satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy adult group. The reported whole-brain results are age-regression analyses across a mixed-age sample (developmental effects), not an unmasked adult-only whole-brain task map; therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map). No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This article reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (self and reflected social attribution/perspective-taking; attribute framing), with healthy adult participants aged 19–41. The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM analyses and multiple group-level contrasts (task vs control; positive vs negative frame; frame-consistent vs inconsistent), with coordinates, statistical thresholds, and cluster-size correction reported. Behavioral and neural results for the healthy sample are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition, analysis), Results (including whole-brain contrasts and coordinates), and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social/empathic processing (EEB paradigm) in healthy adult participants (right-handed female undergraduate samples; fMRI samples N=18 and N=32; total N across experiments reported). Group-level, voxelwise random-effects fMRI analyses are described (whole-brain exploratory analysis in fMRI Experiment 1 and group-level analyses/contrasts in fMRI Experiment 2) with reported coordinates and statistical thresholds; results are presented as whole-brain contrasts and tables of coordinates (and figures). The study is empirical, contains full methods, results, and discussion, and reports healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps (not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only results). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI task explicitly probing social-related processing (social vs. nonsocial gestures) using healthy participants. It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (TFCE and permutation testing; tables/figures reported) for the healthy sample. The sample comprises healthy young adults (mean age 21.41; range 16.9–25.7) and is reported as a healthy/control group (no clinical group-only reporting). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the review. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a social context (collaborative vs competitive effort task) in a sample of healthy adults (N=32, ages 18–39). It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM contrasts and parametric modulators) with reported activation maps, cluster-level FWE correction, peak coordinates, and tables/figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of methods and whole-brain results. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study tests social-related processing (judging ambiguous social interactions) in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 23–39). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts (FDR-corrected), tables/figures of activations (SI, SII, IFG, hippocampus, amygdala, etc.), and correlations with behavior. All core article components (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for social fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps.

This paper reports a voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) study in healthy adults (N=63) examining associations between grey-matter volumes and proneness to moral sentiments. Although the work discusses prior fMRI findings and uses individual SSC-BOLD responses from a subgroup as a secondary covariate, the article does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI activation maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it does not meet the review’s fMRI-specific inclusion requirements. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly examines social processing (trustworthiness, attractiveness judgments) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=44; ages 21–60). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates and figures of activations. All inclusion criteria are met (task is social-related; healthy adult sample within 18–65; whole-brain group-level task activations reported; results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy using task-based fMRI with naturalistic video stimuli, meeting the review objective. Sample: 27 healthy adult participants (mean age 34.1), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts and voxelwise activation maps/coordinates (e.g., contrasts E>N, conjunction analyses, figures showing whole-brain activations), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met. Inclusion IDs satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion IDs satisfied: none.

This empirical fMRI study (healthy adults, N=15, ages 20–28) includes a social-related task (social distance: participants judged familiarity of friends vs acquaintances) implemented during fMRI and analyzed at the group level. The paper reports whole-brain searchlight MVPA and RSA group analyses with voxelwise statistical maps/clusters (FDR-corrected clusters presented and tables/figures of significant clusters), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. All inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses task fMRI of social processing (social closeness judgments) in healthy participants (I3 met). However, the sample mixes adolescents and adults and does not report a separate healthy adult-only group analysis (I4 not met). Critically, the fMRI results are reported as ROI-based analyses (beta extraction from predefined ROIs) rather than providing any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy group; no unmasked whole-brain task maps or coordinate tables for whole-brain contrasts are presented (I5 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because E2 applies; inclusion I3 met, I4 and I5 not met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-, other-, and reflected self-evaluations across social/academic/physical domains), meeting the review's focus on perception/understanding of self and others. The paper reports a healthy adult group (19 adults, ages 22–31) analyzed and reported separately from adolescents. Whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses are reported (SPM8 whole-brain ANOVA, AlphaSim/FWE correction, cluster tables/figures and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group-level maps. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, includes adult subgroup within 18–65, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognitive processing (causal attributions/mentalizing) using a task with social stimuli (I3). The sample is healthy adults aged 18–41 (n=20), meeting the adult healthy sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (each attribution locus > truth baseline), conjunctions, and whole-brain results in tables/figures with appropriate thresholds (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and within-group whole-brain task effects for the healthy sample are explicitly reported. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (attribution of awareness to another), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=50; ages 18–49) with a within-group fMRI task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (H trials − E trials) with corrected thresholding, surface projections, and tables of Talairach coordinates for significant clusters (TPJ and prefrontal regions). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 20.7, N=26) investigating social processes (social exclusion, punishment and forgiveness) using Cyberball and a modified Dictator Game. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., exclusion no-ball > inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality) with tables/figures of activation peaks and cluster results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self- and other-referential recollection) in healthy adults. The Methods report 18 healthy right-handed native English speaking participants aged 19–29. The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation results including whole-brain analyses with cluster coordinates and whole-brain FWE-corrected results (Tables and figures) and ROI SVC results; results are presented for the healthy/control sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The article is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-referential/moral processing in intergroup competition), with healthy adult participants (N=21, ages within 18–65). The paper reports both ROI and whole-brain random-effects analyses, with group-level whole-brain task contrasts and coordinate tables (Tables 1–2 and supplementary figures) using corrected thresholds. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates facial color processing—a form of social communication/perception of others—and thus addresses the review objective. It tested 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.24), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (natural-colored face vs natural-colored scrambled image) and identifies face-selective regions (bilateral FFA and OFA) with coordinates and figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Although ROI analyses are also performed, whole-brain results are reported, so the study is not excluded on ROI-only grounds. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating social feedback processing (self/other trait ratings) during a task involving social interaction and feedback—meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy German and Chinese adults (adult age range implied; no clinical groups), and healthy-group results are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (flexible factorial designs, whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters; coordinates/tables and figures are provided). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (an interactive rating task) in healthy adult participants (mean age ~24) reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked results. The paper presents voxelwise whole-brain analyses with clusterwise FWE correction, tables/figures of activations (e.g., Tables 2–3, figures), and trial-by-trial parametric contrasts related to social partner ratings. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining perception/understanding of others’ social interactions (third-person perspective) in healthy adult participants (10 right-handed males, ages 22–32). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (atypical vs typical displays), with cluster-size correction and tables/coordinates, and describes results and effective connectivity. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), and I6 (results clearly described and reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses an ultimatum game (social interaction) with healthy adult participants (mean age 25) and reports group-level task contrasts; however, all voxelwise analyses were performed within a predefined mask composed of 16 bilateral ROIs rather than as an unmasked whole-brain analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no unmasked whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map was reported). Exclusion criterion met: E2 (analyses restricted to ROI/masked results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The article reports an fMRI experiment using social/empathy-related stimuli (traffic-awareness campaign videos) during task-based scanning, thus addressing a social processing task. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (20 right-handed males, ages 20–28), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (CV > NV) with FWE-corrected results, tables/figures, and ROI follow-up, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without healthy-group task map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates cross-modal person recognition (voice→face) and uses healthy adult participants (n=16, ages 20–31), so it meets I3 (social-related processing) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, all reported significant results are based on ROI/small-volume corrections (FWE corrected for ROIs) and the authors state there were no significant results at P<0.05 FWE for the whole brain without the covariate. The paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (voxelwise) for the healthy group; significant findings are restricted to ROI analyses. Therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on E2.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (social sharing of emotions) in healthy adult participants (female, ages 20–33). Group-level, whole-brain, random-effects analyses are reported (voxelwise contrasts, with whole-brain cluster correction and tables/figures describing activations beyond ROIs). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (repeated public good game) that explicitly investigates social tie formation and prosocial decision-making. Sample includes healthy adult participants (25 scanned participants, mean age 22.6) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and coordinates (cluster-corrected results and MNI coordinates) for multiple contrasts (tie parametric effects, impulse, contribution magnitude), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (participants judged feeling addressed), meeting the review’s focus on social-related processing. Sample: 37 healthy adults (age range 20–39), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (main effects and interactions) with cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates (tables and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social perception using videos of crowds with interactive vs individual dynamics (social-related task). Sample: 16 healthy adults aged 19–27. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVAs), cluster tables, and whole-brain figures describing main effects and interactions. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete.

This is an original fMRI study of social cognition (deception/sophisticated deception, ToM) in healthy adults (n=34, ages 21–32), meeting the review objective. It reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (multiple contrasts: deception vs truth, sophisticated vs simple deception, parametric analyses) with coordinates and tables, and describes full whole-brain preprocessing and Bayesian second-level analyses. Results are presented as voxelwise maps/tables of coordinates (visualization threshold reported). The sample falls within 18–65 and analyses are reported for the healthy group. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical dfMRI study of face-to-face eye contact (a social processing task). Participants: 19 pairs (38 healthy adults), ages 18–33, within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM and paired t-test results (thresholds, cluster sizes), probabilistic atlas labels, cluster tables and MNI coordinates; ICA results are also projected onto whole-brain CCRI masks. Therefore it provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps for healthy adults. Meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social-attributional processing in healthy adults (N=19; ages 21–46). The task manipulates social vs. nonsocial attribution (why/how) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses (conjunctions, interaction contrasts) with cluster-level correction; results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI social task in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level task activation reporting.

This empirical fMRI study investigates social reward processing using a social incentive delay task in healthy adult participants (N=63, ages 20.4–36.6). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results (whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables/figures) for the healthy cohort, including contrasts of social vs monetary reward during anticipation and feedback. Core article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study directly examines social-related processing (social working memory, perspective-taking) using task-based functional MRI (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 21.56), within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, contrasts, cluster tables with coordinates, Figures and Tables 1–2) and describes statistical thresholds and cluster extents, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5). Results and whole-brain findings are described in text, figures and tables (meets I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, pediatric-only, non-empirical, or between-group-only reporting). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4) and it reports voxelwise results/coordinates and figures (meets I6), the group-level statistical analyses reported in the paper are restricted to a bilateral STS mask rather than presented as at least one unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. The Methods explicitly state that second-level/group analyses were restricted to voxels within an STS mask, and results/figures focus on STS-restricted maps. Therefore the study does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that directly probes social-cognitive/mentalizing processing (why/how questions about actions; engages theory-of-mind networks), uses healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (final N=17, ages 21–46), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and cluster-corrected results in the main text and figures. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=37, ages 18–25) that investigates neural correlates of the urge to imitate during a task involving observation and imitation of hand actions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric modulation, PPI) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and provides tables/figures of activations. The task probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others; imitation/ social communication). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (viewing social vs non-social scenes) and measured task-evoked BOLD responses in healthy adults (undergraduates aged 18–21). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (social > non-social) with FDR-corrected statistical maps and cluster results presented in figures and a table, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind using animated triangles), in a healthy adult sample (n=20; age range 24–64 years). The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ToM > R, ToM > Baseline) with statistical thresholds, tables/figures of activations and coordinate peaks, and correlation/Bayesian analyses. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related tasks in healthy adults and provides the required whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15 initial, N=14 analyzed; all males, mean age 23.6) who viewed realistic two-person violent interactions — a clearly social task involving perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., all conditions vs. baseline; focus on aggressor vs. focus on victim) with statistical maps and supplementary tables, and describes whole-brain connectivity analyses. Results for the healthy/control group are reported directly. Therefore the study satisfies the review’s fMRI/social-task requirement, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=26, ages 19–26) while participants read passages varying in social content, addressing social-cognitive processing. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates reported (Table 1), and also ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly identified for the healthy sample. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present).

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) and reports task-evoked whole-brain analyses (exclusion vs inclusion) across healthy adult participants (unmarried university students). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts (with FWE correction) and tables/figures of activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only connectivity-only reporting, and participants are healthy adults within the age range).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social perception (racial in-group/out-group face processing and disgust perception) using a task-based passive viewing paradigm, meeting the review objective. Sample: healthy adults (N=26 analyzed; mean age ~21) within 18–65. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses are reported (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA, contrasts and corrected cluster results; coordinates and figures are provided), and whole-brain results are described in text and tables. Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity, it additionally provides unmasked whole-brain task activation maps and ROI follow-ups. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This fMRI study examines comprehension of speech acts (Naming vs Requesting), a social-communication task relevant to social processing. Participants were healthy adults (n=18 analyzed, ages 18–41). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with FDR-corrected results (e.g., “Request > Naming” at p<0.05 FDR) and provides tables/figures of these results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Dynamic Social Gestures) probing social vs. nonsocial gesture processing and related factors (I3). The sample is a healthy young adult group (mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7) reported and analyzed as a healthy group (I4) — although one participant is just under 18, the reported analyses are for the healthy sample as a whole. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) and provides tabled peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying whole-brain reporting and coordinate reporting requirements (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nor non-empirical, and a healthy adult group is analyzed. Full text is complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=26; mean age 28.7) that uses task-based functional MRI during social tasks (face-viewing, person-judgment) probing perception/understanding of others and affiliation-related processes. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, random-effects parametric analyses linking neural activity to targets’ sociometric popularity (see whole-brain results, Fig. S1 and Table S4) and describes voxelwise group-level effects (FWE-corrected). Independent localizers and ROI analyses are also used, but whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy sample are explicitly reported. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI).

This is an empirical fMRI study (MVPA/RSA) in healthy adult participants (N=20; ages 18–27) using a social cognition task (thinking about others’ mental states). The paper reports group-level whole-brain searchlight and network analyses with random-effects t tests and cluster-corrected voxelwise maps (figures/tables and supplementary material), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The task probes perception/understanding of others (social-related processing). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social learning (participants learned about other people’s generosity) using healthy adult participants (N=30 recruited, 26 included; ages 19–37). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests, voxel-wise thresholding and whole-brain cluster correction), with coordinates and tables/figures provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results clearly reported in maps/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment investigating person perception and person knowledge (social cognition) using task-based fMRI. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=21; mean age 24.6 years) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (univariate analyses and PPI), with results described in text, figures, and tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of theory-of-mind/social processing in a healthy adult sample (n=24; mean age 25.7). The task included social story conditions (agent-behavior and agent-mental) and a ToM functional localizer, conducted during fMRI. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster coordinates for contrasts (e.g., social > non-social during Background; unexpected > expected during Outcome) and provides tables of peak MNI coordinates. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social-related task; I4: healthy adult participants 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported; I6: whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball ball-toss) that examines neural responses to social interaction frequency. Participants were healthy adults (ages ~21; N=31 analyzed), meeting the age and sample requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (ball-toss high-frequency > normal-frequency; contrasts versus button-press) with cluster-level FWE correction and peak coordinates (ventral striatum, precuneus), satisfying whole-brain reporting. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports whole-brain task-based fMRI of a social interaction paradigm (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) in a healthy adult sample (N=15 males, mean age 22.3). Group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables are reported (figures and Talairach coordinates), and parametric modulation analyses are presented. This meets the meta-analysis objective of social-related fMRI in healthy adults and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with background, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy and perspective taking) in healthy adults (N=33, ages 20–34). The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked analyses (searchlight MVPA and GLM contrasts) with group-level voxelwise results and peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. It clearly meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a validated social cognition task (EmpaToM) manipulating empathy and Theory of Mind (ToM), reporting behavioral and neural results. Sample: 178 healthy adults (mean age 40.9, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (emotional > neutral videos for empathy; ToM > non-ToM questions/videos) with voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates/tables, and describes resting-state and DCM analyses in addition to task activations. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This article reports an fMRI study of social cognition (impression updating), using a task that probes perception/understanding of others. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=21, ages 18–31). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (e.g., L2>F3 whole-brain contrasts, 2×4 ANOVA, cluster-corrected results with tables/figures listing coordinates and clusters). Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, empirical with original fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants (n=34, mean age 22.2) watched a movie while BOLD was recorded and the paper probes neural responses to social interactions. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task: naturalistic movie viewing assessing social interactions), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65), and I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation maps and statistical parametric maps—see whole-brain reverse correlation analysis and Fig. 3, with corrected thresholds). I6 (whole-brain results presented as figures/statistics) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes a within-group/common-group task effect, participants are adults, and it is an empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports an fMRI task probing social-related processing (observation of others’ actions in emotional contexts—anger vs. joy), satisfying the review’s construct scope. Sample includes 20 healthy adults (ages 23–33), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., main effects and AG>joyful contrasts) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This paper reports original fMRI experiments using social tasks (Prisoner’s Dilemma, Ultimatum/Welfare Game) manipulating sociality, meeting the review’s definition of social-related processing (I3). Samples are healthy adults (college/community; ages ≥18) with results reported separately for the healthy group (I4). The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses using mixed-effects FSL (FLAME) and SPM12 random-effects, with thresholded statistical maps and tables of coordinates (e.g., Table 4) and cluster-level results—satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete=false not set). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, age out of range, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=25, ages 19–26) using an attachment appraisal task (social/attachment processing). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (attachment vs. neutral) with cluster-level correction and MNI coordinates, clearly attributable to the healthy sample. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task activation in healthy adults and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (self/other, cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adults. Methods, results (including behavioral and fMRI analyses), and discussion are present in the full text. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=24; ages 19–31) satisfying the age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and cluster-corrected whole-brain results (e.g., pgACC and area 9 whole-brain effects), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social task (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma; I3), includes a healthy adult sample (female university participants, mean age 21; I4), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction for contrasts (CC vs others, gain vs loss, interaction) fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, tables of coordinates, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (N=38, ages 18–30) using a social-related task (Social Detection Task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (2×3×2 ANOVA) and presents whole-brain task activation results (FWE-corrected, Table 1, figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotion regulation using angry facial expressions (a social stimulus), meeting the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=60, age range 18–57; resting-state N=48), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry; Increase vs Observe-angry; whole-brain results summarized in figures and tables) clearly identified for the healthy group. Whole-brain results are reported in tables and described in text. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI during a social/prosocial learning task; (I4) the sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=31, ages 19–32); (I5) group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (flexible-factorial second-level model with reported statistical maps, tables, and figures corresponding to the healthy group); (I6) whole-brain results and coordinates are presented in figures/tables (Figs. 2–3, Tables S1–S4). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social mentalizing task about friends vs kin, with healthy adult participants (n=25 females, mean age 23.2), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and linear parametric analyses (friend > kin contrasts, parametric maps across network layers) with cluster-corrected coordinates and figures. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related Face Matching Task (fearful and neutral faces) during task fMRI (meets I3). The sample is ten healthy adults aged within 18–65 and reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests at the second level) and presents results in tables/figures/supplement (meets I5 and I6). Although ICA connectivity analyses are included, whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group are reported, so no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions; therefore fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI study of social competition (a social-related task involving social comparison/mentalizing). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (20 females aged 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., competition > no-competition; performance-related parametric modulators) with cluster-correction and peak coordinates reported in text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion criterion met: E4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (STRESS > CONTROL and conjunctions) and ROI analyses, but does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (e.g., a within-group INJECTION > QTIP or BIOPSY > QTIP map for the control group or the full healthy sample). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related empathy-for-pain task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–40 reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present; supplementary material noted but not required). Because I5 is not satisfied and exclusion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 21–46) that investigates social cognitive processing (attribution/understanding of others’ emotions for humans and non-human animals). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (Explicit Task Emotion>Expression contrasts and Implicit Task Face>Scramble contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and presents whole-brain statistical maps and ROI and whole-brain results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample reported separately; I5: group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported; I6: whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (face emotion and age judgments), with healthy adult participants (final N=25, ages 21–33). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (univariate random-effects contrast faces>objects and whole-brain searchlight analyses with SnPM correction) and provides tables/figures describing whole-brain results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study includes a healthy adult group (ages 20–41) performing a social-related task (social interaction recognition from point-light displays). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (SI > NM) for the adult group with voxelwise results, cluster- and peak-level statistics, and figures/tables describing activations (including FWE-corrected clusters). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports fMRI data collected while participants read news headlines/abstracts and considered sharing—engaging social cognition/mentalizing relevant to social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (ages 18–24). The paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain maps/tables (SI Fig. S3, Table S5) for the healthy samples. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (two cohorts, n=24 and n=26; ages in reported means 20–23, within 18–65) performing social/person-knowledge retrieval tasks, which fall under social-related processing (Perception/Understanding of Others). Group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM results are reported (contrasts such as all memory > baseline, status > baseline, trait > baseline) with voxelwise FWE-corrected maps and coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of mentalising (theory-of-mind) tasks — a social-cognition paradigm — in healthy adult participants (Experiment 2: N=17, mean age 22, right-handed, no neurological/psychiatric history). The authors conducted whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses and report voxelwise contrasts (e.g., mentalising > factual; parametric modulation) with thresholding and a full coordinate table (Table 1) and figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The task clearly targets perception/understanding of others (social processing). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-evoked fMRI in healthy adults (N=41; ages 18–24) while participants made social-related judgments (decisions to share/select articles; includes narrowcast to a specific friend), directly addressing social communication and perception of others/self. The paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses (select > content, share > content, share > select) with family-wise error correction and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures, meeting requirements for voxelwise healthy-group task activation. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, is empirical). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults (N=22 analyzed; mean age 24.4). The study used task-based fMRI during social-related stimuli (implicit/explicit belief/Sally–Anne paradigms), meeting the review’s topical requirement. The paper reports a whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM contrast (false-belief vs false-photograph) used to localize explicit ToM ROIs, with voxelwise results and Talairach peak coordinates reported at q(FDR)<0.05; thus it provides whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps (reported in text/figure/tables of coordinates). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of theory-of-mind (mentalizing) using verbal narratives in healthy adult participants, so it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65). However, the reported analyses focus on ROI-based MVPA and individually-defined ROIs/localizer contrasts; the full text does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy/control group (unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effects) in the main paper or described figures/tables. Therefore it fails I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Based on the provided full text (which appears complete), I exclude the study for not reporting the required whole-brain group-level task activation maps. If supplementary materials contain unreported group maps, inclusion could be reconsidered, but they are not available here.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social interaction perception (social/third-party interaction processing), meeting the review’s focus on social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (n=14, ages 20–32) so sample criterion is met. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (surface-based group maps, peak MNI coordinates, figures, and supplementary figures/tables) showing activation contrasts (interaction > independent, animate > physical, etc.), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and supplementary materials. The full paper includes Introduction, Methods (participants, acquisition, preprocessing, analyses), Results, and Discussion; full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (60 White men, mean age 23.8) using a task that requires social perception/evaluation (impression formation of faces varying in race and socioeconomic status), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (exploratory whole-brain regressions for main effects and correlations with EMS; a VMPFC cluster is reported and Supplementary Material contains full whole-brain results), satisfying whole-brain evidence criteria. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants judged orientation (facing toward/away) of point-light and human-like walkers, a task probing perception/understanding of others (meets I3). Sample comprises 16 healthy adults (mean age 22.75), within 18–65 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts with stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1) and thresholding details (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references; no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants in range, empirical data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study used fMRI of social/attachment narratives in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4) but does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map from the healthy/control group. The neuroimaging results are resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity analyses (caudate nucleus) comparing baseline and post-narrative rest scans. Therefore it falls under exclusion E3 (only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI during social/attachment-related paradigm) and I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social interactions (cooperative vs affective) in 36 healthy adult participants (ages ~24–25). It includes whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (parametric and categorical contrasts with cluster-level FDR correction, tables and coordinates) and clearly-identified healthy-group results. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (joint action, leading/following, mutuality) using healthy adult dancers (N=18, mean age 40.4) and clearly addresses social-cognitive processes (mentalizing, social reward, perception of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts, Talairach coordinates, FDR-corrected maps, and tables of peak activations), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

The paper reports task-based fMRI including an explicit social cognition task (TOM vs Random), uses a large healthy adult sample (n=787; ages 22–>35 within 18–65 range), and presents group-level whole-brain task activation maps (HCP level 2/3 maps transformed to Cohen's d and visualized in figures/tables). Results for the healthy/control group are reported and clearly described. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (modified iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–38). The task is clearly social (perception/understanding of others; ToM), satisfying I3. The sample is within 18–65 and healthy, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (conjunction analyses, COMP>COOP contrasts, cluster-level corrected results, tables/figures with peak coordinates and percent signal change), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

Empirical fMRI study directly comparing social vs. non-social stimuli (social-related task), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=14 analyzed, ages 23–50) screened for psychiatric disorders, and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (social > non-social contrast) with figures/tables and thresholding details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).
