This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (university students aged 19–24 and 19.67 in Study 2) that uses task-based fMRI to investigate emotion perception (facial and vocal), which is a social-cognition/social-communication task (perception and understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA, whole-brain contrasts, PFWE-corrected results, and tables/figures of activated regions) for the healthy sample. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). I3 is satisfied: study used fMRI during a social-related task (choices free vs controlled by another person; investigates social cognitions/control aversion). I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) cannot be confirmed because ages are not reported in the provided content. I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the abstract; the abstract emphasizes functional connectivity findings but does not clearly state whole-brain task activation maps. Because essential inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included at this stage. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on available information.

Only the article abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract, the study uses fMRI to investigate prosodic cues for social communicative intentions, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) appears met. However, key information to verify other inclusion criteria is missing: participant ages/sample details (I4) are not reported in the abstract, and it is not possible to confirm that the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map (I5). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete and I4 and I5 cannot be verified, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation), satisfying the review objective. It tested healthy adult participants (n=31, ages 19–24) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (contrasts, tables of coordinates, figures; voxel-wise p<0.001, cluster-level FWE p<0.05). Whole-brain regression and PPI analyses are reported and healthy-group task effects (e.g., SA vs. Fixation; SC vs. SA) are clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study includes a social cognition (theory-of-mind) task among others, uses task fMRI in healthy adult samples (HCP: ages 22–36; UCLA: 21–50), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results (voxel-wise GLM and activation maps/figures) for the healthy participants. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5; whole-brain results are also presented in figures/supplementary material, satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text unavailable (404 Not Found); only metadata/title/DOI present. All core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not between-group-only comparisons, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, do not report only connectivity/resting-state, and include healthy-group whole-brain activation maps. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (live bidirectional conversation; human–human vs human–robot), reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM, FDR-corrected results) including contrasts HHI vs HRI and main effects. Sample includes 21 healthy adults (age mean 25.8) within 18–65. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review's inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (empathy/perception of human vs. robot in pain/pleasure) and directly addresses social-related processing. The sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–27, reported separately (N=26 final). The paper includes group-level whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses (repetition-suppression and discrete event-related contrasts), cluster-corrected results, and provides whole-brain group maps (NeuroVault) and detailed tables—meeting whole-brain evidence reporting requirements. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of dynamic facial-expression processing (a social communication task) in a sample of healthy adults (n=51, mean age 22.5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs) with FWE-corrected thresholds and presents results in text, tables, and figures. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study of vocal emotional processing uses task-evoked fMRI in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4) and the full text is provided. However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps or coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain activation for the healthy group. Analyses are ROI/parcellation-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical metrics (Power-264 ROIs), i.e., ROI-level connectivity results only. Therefore it meets exclusion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) and related I6 (acceptable formats of whole-brain results) are not satisfied. Exclude on that basis.
